1: # About the WhatsApp Business Platform
2: The WhatsApp Business Platform enables businesses to communicate with customers at scale.
3: This documentation is intended for developers using our APIs. If you are looking for information on other ways to use WhatsApp for your business see the [WhatsApp Business site](https://business.whatsapp.com/).
4: ## Core APIs and capabilities
5: ### WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API
6: The WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API enables you to programmatically message and call on WhatsApp. You can use Cloud API to send users a variety of messages, from simple text messages to rich media and interactive messages.
7: Cloud API includes:
8: * **Messaging:** Send text messages, rich media, and interactive messages
9: * **Calling:** Make and receive calls to customers
10: * **Groups:** Create, manage, and message WhatsApp group conversations
11: WhatsApp messaging lets you send encrypted messages to customers. Use Cloud API to:
12: * Send order confirmations and shipping updates
13: * Share appointment availability and other reminders
14: * Send messages that recommend related or additional products
15: * Facilitate end-to-end transactions, from product discovery to payment
16: * Enable multi-factor authentication or one-time passwords to verify accounts and users
17: * Deliver custom interactive conversational experiences
18: [Learn more about message types on Cloud API.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages)
19: ### WhatsApp Business Platform Business Management API
20: The WhatsApp Business Management API enables you to programmatically manage your WhatsApp platform assets:
21: * **WhatsApp account management:** Create accounts, add and remove phone numbers, link accounts together, and assign partner access.
22: * **Messaging account management:** Create accounts, manage templates for scalable messaging, and configure billing and payment methods.
23: Business Management API also gives you access to account analytics like:
24: * **Messaging analytics:** The number and type of messages sent and delivered.
25: * **Pricing analytics:** Granular pricing breakdowns for delivered messages.
26: * **Template analytics:** Sent/read/delivered template metrics, alongside template message button clicks.
27: - [Learn more about message templates.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/overview)
28: - [Learn more about managing business phone numbers.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-phone-numbers/phone-numbers)
29: - [Learn more about account analytics.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/analytics)
30: ### Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp
31: MM API for WhatsApp is an API for sending optimized marketing messages on WhatsApp.
32: When you send marketing messages through the MM API for WhatsApp, you can access new features not available on Cloud API and get automatic optimizations, so high engagement messages can reach more customers.
33: The MM API for WhatsApp includes:
34: * **Quality-based delivery:** Up to 9% higher marketing message deliveries over Cloud API for high engagement content.
35: * **Automated creative optimizations:** Automatic enhancements to marketing creative to increase message performance.
36: * **Performance benchmarks and recommendations:** Comparison of read and click rates versus similar templates from businesses in your region.
37: * **Conversion metrics:** Measure marketing messages that lead users to perform app events such as 'Add to Cart', 'Checkout Initiated', or 'Purchase'.
38: [Learn more about the Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/marketing-messages/overview)
39: ### Webhooks
40: Webhooks deliver JSON payloads to your server for message status updates, incoming messages, asynchronous error handling, and many other notification utilities.
41: The platform relies heavily on webhooks, as the contents of any message sent from a WhatsApp user to your business phone number is communicated via webhook, and all outgoing message delivery status updates are reported via webhook.
42: [Learn more about webhooks](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/overview).
43: ### Meta Business Agent
44: Meta Business Agent lets you configure and operate AI-powered agents on WhatsApp. Agents handle conversations with WhatsApp users autonomously, using knowledge sources you provide (FAQs, business info, product catalogs, files, and websites) and custom connectors to your external APIs.
45: Meta Business Agent includes:
46: * **Agent configuration:** Set agent behavior, persona, language, and system instructions
47: * **Knowledge management:** Connect FAQs, business info, catalogs, files, and websites for the agent to reference
48: * **Custom connectors:** Integrate your external APIs so the agent can take actions like checking order status or booking appointments
49: * **Thread control:** Manage handoffs between the AI agent and human agents
50: * **Evaluation and testing:** Test agent responses and evaluate performance
51: [Learn more about Meta Business Agent](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/meta-business-agent/get-started).
52: ## Technical foundations
53: ### HTTP protocol and API requests
54: The WhatsApp Business Platform is built on [Graph API](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview) and uses HTTP protocol. API requests include path, body, and header parameters.
55: #### Example: Sending a text message using cURL
56: ```curl
57: curl 'https://graph.facebook.com/v17.0/106540352242922/messages' \
58: -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
59: -H 'Authorization: Bearer EAAJB...' \
60: -d '{
61: "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
62: "recipient_type": "individual",
63: "to": "+16505555555",
64: "type": "text",
65: "text": {
66: "preview_url": true,
67: "body": "Here's the info you requested! https://www.meta.com/quest/quest-3/"
68: }
69: }'
70: ```
71: [Learn more about the Graph API.](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api)
72: ### JSON responses
73: API responses are formatted in JSON.
74: #### Example: Requesting a business phone number's metadata
75: ```curl
76: {
77: "verified_name": "Lucky Shrub",
78: "code_verification_status": "VERIFIED",
79: "display_phone_number": "15550783881",
80: "quality_rating": "GREEN",
81: "platform_type": "CLOUD_API",
82: "throughput": {
83: "level": "STANDARD"
84: },
85: "webhook_configuration": {
86: "application": "https://www.luckyshrub.com/webhooks"
87: },
88: "id": "106540352242922"
89: }
90: ```
91: ### Authentication and authorization
92: Authentication uses OAuth (not 2.0) access tokens, while permissions restrict access to specific resources.
93: - [Learn more about access tokens.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/access-tokens)
94: - [Learn more about permissions.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/permissions)
95: ## Key resources
96: ### Business portfolios
97: A business portfolio allows organizations to bring all their Meta business assets together so they can be managed in one place. On the WhatsApp Business Platform, a business portfolio mainly serves as a container for your WhatsApp accounts and Messaging accounts. You must have a business portfolio to use the platform.
98: Business portfolios can be verified, and verification status factors into improved functionality, such as higher throughput and [Official Business Account](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/official-business-accounts) status.
99: [Learn more about business portfolios.](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/486932075688253)
100: ### WhatsApp accounts and Messaging accounts {#whatsapp-business-accounts}
101: The WhatsApp Business Platform uses two core account types:
102: * **WhatsApp account (WAAC)** — Your business presence on WhatsApp. Contains your phone numbers, display name, usernames, and partner access configuration. You can link multiple WhatsApp accounts together to share access with partners.
103: * **Messaging account** — Manages your message templates, billing, and payment methods. Each Messaging account can be associated with one or more WhatsApp accounts.
104: Both are associated with your business portfolio (Meta Business Suite).
105: #### Requirements
106: * A [business portfolio](https://business.facebook.com/)
107: * A **WhatsApp account**, associated with your business portfolio (manages phone numbers and business presence)
108: * A **Messaging account**, associated with your business portfolio (manages templates and billing)
109: * A [business app](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/create-an-app/app-dashboard/app-types#business), associated with your business portfolio
110: * Appropriate access tokens and permissions (see [Authentication and authorization](#authentication-and-authorization))
111: **Guidelines for Partners and Agencies:** You have the option to either utilize the shared Messaging account provided to you or create a new Messaging account of your own to link with a client's shared WhatsApp account.
112: [Learn more about WhatsApp accounts and Messaging accounts.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/whatsapp-business-accounts)
113: ### Business phone numbers
114: Business phone numbers, real, or virtual, are used for sending and receiving WhatsApp messages. They can have display names and earn Official Business Account status.
115: [Learn more about business phone numbers.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-phone-numbers/phone-numbers)
116: ### Message templates
117: Templates are customizable messages that you can construct in advance of sending them. Template messages generally require approval before you can send them.
118: Templates are useful for messaging at scale. They are also the only type of message that can be sent to WhatsApp users outside of a [customer service window](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#customer-service-windows).
119: Templates have quality scores and are subject to various messaging limits.
120: [Learn more about message templates.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/overview)
121: ### Test resources
122: When you [get started with Cloud API](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/get-started), a test WhatsApp account, test Messaging account, and test business phone number are automatically created for you. Test accounts and test phone numbers are useful for testing purposes, as they have relaxed messaging limits and don't require a payment method on file in order to send template messages.
123: You can delete your business portfolio and its test resources if:
124: * You are an admin on the business portfolio associated with the app
125: * No other apps are associated with the business portfolio
126: * The business portfolio is not associated with any other WhatsApp accounts or Messaging accounts
127: * The WhatsApp account is not associated with any other business phone numbers.
128: To delete your business portfolio and its test resources:
129: 1. Go to the **App Dashboard > WhatsApp > Configuration** panel.
130: 2. Locate the **Test Account** section.
131: 3. Click the **Delete** button.
132: Use the API Playground when testing endpoints. Find the playground in the "API Reference" section on the left sidebar of this page. In each reference, click the "Try it" button to open the playground.
133: Also helpful for testing is our [Postman collection](https://www.postman.com/meta/whatsapp-business-platform/).
134: ## Tools and integrations
135: ### WhatsApp Manager
136: WhatsApp Manager is a web app for managing Messaging accounts, phone numbers, templates, and reviewing analytics.
137: [Access WhatsApp Manager](https://business.facebook.com/wa/manage/home/)
138: ### Third-party SDKs
139: Some SDKs, like [PyWa](https://pywa.readthedocs.io/en/2.0.1/) (Python wrapper), are available but are not maintained or endorsed by Meta.
140: ### Postman collection
141: The official Postman collection lets you execute common API queries.
142: [Access the WhatsApp Business Platform Postman collection](https://www.postman.com/meta/whatsapp-business-platform/).
143: ## Security and performance
144: ### Throughput
145: Business phone numbers can send up to 80 messages per second by default, with capacity upgrades available.
146: [Learn more about throughput.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/throughput)
147: ### Encryption
148: With Cloud API, every WhatsApp message continues to be protected by Signal protocol encryption that secures messages before they leave the device. Signal protocol encryption ensures that messages with a WhatsApp account are securely delivered to the destination chosen by each business.
149: Cloud API uses industry standard encryption techniques to protect data in transit and at rest. Cloud API uses Graph API for sending messages and Webhooks for receiving events, and both operate over industry standard HTTPS, protected by TLS.
150: See the [WhatsApp Encryption Overview technical whitepaper](https://www.whatsapp.com/security/WhatsApp-Security-Whitepaper.pdf) for additional details.
151: ### Scaling
152: The Cloud API automatically scales usage within your rate limits.
153: ### Rate limits
154: Requests made by your app on your Messaging account are counted against your app's request count. An app's request count is the number of requests it can make during a rolling one hour.
155: For the following endpoints, your app can make 200 requests per hour, per app, per Messaging account, by default. For active Messaging accounts whose WhatsApp account hierarchy has at least one registered phone number, your app can make 5000 requests per hour, per app, per active Messaging account.
156: | Type of request | Endpoint |
157: | --- | --- |
158: | `GET` | `/<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID>` |
159: | `GET`, `POST`, and `DELETE` | `/<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID>/assigned_users` |
160: | `GET` | `/<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID>/phone_numbers` |
161: | `GET`, `POST`, and `DELETE` | `/<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID>/message_templates` |
162: | `GET`, `POST`, and `DELETE` | `/<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID>/subscribed_apps` |
163: | `GET` | `/<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_TO_NUMBER_CURRENT_STATUS_ID>` |
164: For the following [Credit Line API](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/share-and-revoke-credit-lines) requests, your app can make 5000 requests per hour.
165: | Type of request | Endpoint |
166: | --- | --- |
167: | `GET` | `/<BUSINESS_ID>/extendedcredits` |
168: | `POST` | `/<EXTENDED_CREDIT_ID>/whatsapp_credit_sharing_and_attach` |
169: | `GET` and `DELETE` | `/<ALLOCATION_CONFIG_ID>` |
170: | `GET` | `/<EXTENDED_CREDIT_ID>/owning_credit_allocation_configs` |
171: For more information on how to get your current rate usage, see [Headers](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/rate-limiting#headers).
172: In addition, the platform applies several message rate limits:
173: * **Messaging limits:** The maximum number of unique WhatsApp users you can deliver messages to, outside of a customer service window, within a moving 24-hour period. Set at the business portfolio level. See [Messaging limits](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messaging-limits).
174: * **Throughput:** Business phone numbers can send up to 80 messages per second by default, with capacity upgrades available. Set per business phone number. See [Throughput](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/throughput).
175: * **Quality rating:** Assigned per business phone number and per template, and used to determine automatic throughput tier upgrades. See [Template quality rating](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/template-quality).
176: #### Pair rate limits
177: Business phone numbers can send 1 message every 6 seconds to the same WhatsApp user (0.17 messages/second), which equals about 10 messages per minute or 600 per hour. Exceeding this limit triggers [error code 131056](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/support/error-codes#throttling-errors) until you are back within the allowed rate.
178: You may send up to 45 messages in a 6-second burst, but this "borrows" from your future quota. After a burst, you must wait the equivalent time it would take to send those messages at the normal rate (for example, a burst of 20 requires a ~2-minute wait before sending more to that user).
179: To manage post-burst throttling, if a send request fails, retry after 4^X seconds (starting with X=0 and increasing X by 1 after each failure) until successful.
180: ## Terms and policies
181: ### User opt-in
182: You must obtain user [opt-in](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/getting-opt-in) before sending message templates. Opt-in must clarify your business name and intent.
183: [Learn more about the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy.](https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-policy/)
184: ### Terms and policies
185: All WhatsApp Business Platform use must comply with our terms and policies. Using unauthorized third-party tools is prohibited.
186: - [Learn more about terms and policies.](https://whatsappbusiness.com/terms-and-conditions/)
187: ## Next steps
188: [Get started with the WhatsApp Business Platform.](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/get-started)
189: **Learn more**
190: * [Display names](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/display-names)
191: * [Phone numbers](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-phone-numbers/phone-numbers)
192: * [Pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing)
193: * [Webhooks](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/overview)
194: ---
195: Full documentation index for this product: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/llms.txt

1: # WhatsApp Cloud API Get Started
2: **Warning:** This documentation is for developers building on the WhatsApp Business Platform. If you are a WhatsApp user experiencing issues with your personal account, visit the [WhatsApp Help Center](https://faq.whatsapp.com/) for support.
3: This guide helps developers quickly get started with the WhatsApp Cloud API. It covers the basic setup steps, including registering as a developer, creating a Meta app, sending your first message, and setting up a test webhook endpoint. You'll also learn how to generate secure access tokens and send both template and non-template messages. Advanced features and further resources are introduced for deeper exploration.
4: ---
5: ## Download the sample app
6: The Jasper's Market sample app contains all of the messages and code used in the Jasper's Market demo. You can use this sample app to learn how to build an application that sends and handles WhatsApp Cloud API data.
7: [Download the Jasper's Market Sample App](https://github.com/fbsamples/whatsapp-business-jaspers-market)
8: ---
9: ## Prerequisites
10: - Facebook account or managed Meta account
11: - Developer registration
12: - If not yet registered, visit the [developer registration page](https://developers.facebook.com/async/registration/) and follow the prompts.
13: - WhatsApp-enabled device for sending and receiving test messages
14: ---
15: ## Step 1. Create a new Meta app with WhatsApp
16: 1. Open the [Meta App Dashboard](https://developers.facebook.com/apps) to create a new Meta app with the WhatsApp use case.
17: 2. Click **Create App**.
18: 3. Add your app's name and your email.
19: 4. Select the **Connect with customers through WhatsApp** use case and click **Next**.
20: 5. Select an existing business portfolio or create a new one.
21: 6. A list of publishing requirements are listed. You may not have any at this point. Click **Next**.
22: 7. Confirm your details, use case, and business portfolio. Click **Previous** to make changes or **Create app** to complete app creation.
23: After creating your app with the WhatsApp use case you are redirected to the **Customize use case > Connect on WhatsApp > Quickstart** page in the dashboard.
24: ## Step 2. Start using the API
25: 1. Click the **Start using the API** button to set up the API by adding a phone number and sending your first message. You are redirected to the **API Setup** page.
26: 2. In the **API Setup** section, connect your app to a Messaging account. This connection allows your app to access the WhatsApp Cloud API and send messages on behalf of your business. Select an existing Messaging account or create a new one:
27: - **To use an existing account:** Select the Messaging account from the dropdown menu.
28: - **To create a new account:** Click **Create a WhatsApp Business account** and follow the prompts to set up your business profile.
29: 5. Once connected, you will see your Messaging account ID displayed in the API Setup panel.
30: - Save this ID for use in API calls.
31: > **Note:** If you created a new Meta Business Portfolio during app creation, a Messaging account may have been automatically created for you. Verify the connection in the API Setup section before proceeding.
32: ---
33: ## Step 3. Send and receive messages
34: 1. Click **Generate access token** to generate a temporary access token to send a test message.
35: 2. Select a **From** phone number, or add a new one, from the dropdown menu.
36: 3. Add a **To** phone number that will receive the test message.
37: 4. Click the **Send message** button to send your first message.
38: - Make sure to retain both your test phone number ID and Messaging account ID for later use.
39: 4. Once you receive the message you sent, make sure to reply back to keep the conversation going.
40: The left-side menu lists ways in which you can customize use case settings and permissions to make your app work the way you want it to. You can update these settings at any time.
41: - [**Permissions and features**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#permissions-and-features) - View required and optional permissions for this use case and add them to an App Review submission, if applicable.
42: - [**Quickstart**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#quickstart) - Start using the API and learn how to scale your business, improve ROI, and manage your Messaging account.
43: - [**API Setup**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#api-setup) - Generate access tokens, send and receive messages, and configure webhooks and the WhatsApp SDK.
44: - [**Configuration**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#configuration) - Configure webhooks and the WhatsApp SDK.
45: - [**Resources**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#resources) – View the WhatsApp developer documentation, Meta Blueprint courses, and support resources.
46: - [**Tech Provider onboarding**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#tech-provider-onboarding) – Start scaling the WhatsApp Business Platform for your business.
47: - [**Partner Solutions**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#partner-solutions) – Create a partner solution.
48: - [**Embedded Signup Builder**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/development/create-an-app/whatsapp-use-case#embedded-signup-builder) – Integrate Embedded Signup flow into your website or client portal.
49: ---
50: ## Step 4. Set up the test webhook app
51: You will need to set up a webhook endpoint in order to receive notifications about message statuses, such as read and delivered.
52: Use the sample webhook server for testing purposes by following the [Using a test webhook app](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/set-up-whatsapp-echo-bot) guide.
53: Once your test webhook application is established, respond in the WhatsApp chat thread you created with yourself. You will see the webhook payload in your test application like this:
54: ```json
55: {
56: "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
57: "entry": [
58: {
59: "id": "215589313241560883",

85: }
86: ]

89: }
90: ]
91: }

93: }
94: ```
95: ---
96: ## Step 5. Create a system user and generate a permanent access token
97: The temporary access token you created to send the `hello_world` template message expires quickly and is not suitable for development purposes.
98: So you should create a permanent token for use across the WhatsApp Business Platform.
99: 1. Navigate to [Business Settings](https://business.facebook.com/latest/settings) and click **System users** in the sidebar.
100: 2. Click the **Add+** button in the upper-right corner and follow the prompts to create a new system user.
101: 3. Select the new system user you created, and click **Assign Assets.**
102: - Select your app and toggle **Manage app** under **Full control.**
103: - Select your WhatsApp account and toggle **Manage WhatsApp Business accounts** under **Full control.**
104: - Click the **Assign assets** button.
105: 4. Click **Generate token.**
106: - Follow the prompts to generate your token.
107: - Add the following permissions to the token:
108: - [business_management](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions#b)
109: - [whatsapp_business_messaging](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions#w)
110: - [whatsapp_business_management](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions#w)
111: - Copy the token and store it in a secure place to be used in the later steps.
112: ---
113: ## Step 6. Send a non-template message
114: When you responded to your earlier test message, you triggered what is known as a [customer service window](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#customer-service-windows). This 24-hour window allows you to send [non-template messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#message-types) to users on WhatsApp. With the customer service window now open, you can send a non-template message to yourself.
115: To do this, insert your test phone number ID, the system user access token, and your phone number in the code sample below, then paste the code into your terminal and run it.
116: ```bash
117: curl 'https://graph.facebook.com/v23.0/<TEST_BUSINESS_PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages' \
118: -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
119: -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SYSTEM_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN>' \
120: -d '
121: {
122: "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
123: "recipient_type": "individual",
124: "to": "<WHATSAPP_USER_PHONE_NUMBER>",
125: "type": "text",
126: "text": {
127: "body": "Hello!"
128: }
129: }'
130: ```
131: After successfully sending your message, check your test webhook application to view the webhook event confirming the message receipt.
132: If you don't have a user's phone number, you can send to their [business-scoped user ID (BSUID)](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-scoped-user-ids) by replacing `to` with `recipient`. See [Send to a BSUID](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#send-to-a-bsuid).
133: ---
134: ## Step 7. Finish
135: The WhatsApp Cloud API enables you to send messages and receive webhooks—these are the fundamental building blocks for messaging integration.
136: Beyond these basics, the API offers additional features such as group creation and management, as well as support for calling.
137: To explore these advanced capabilities, check out the "Learn more" section below.
138: ---
139: ## Learn more
140: - [Learn about the different types of non-template messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages)
141: - [Learn how to create and send template messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/overview)
142: - [Learn how to create and manage WhatsApp groups via API](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups)
143: - [Learn how to send and receive calls on WhatsApp via API](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/calling)
144: - [Learn how to add a business phone number](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-phone-numbers/phone-numbers)
145: - [Learn how to set up your own webhook server](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/webhooks/getting-started)
146: - [Onboard WhatsApp Business app users](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/onboarding-business-app-users) — allow businesses already using the WhatsApp Business app to connect their existing account and phone number to Cloud API via Embedded Signup
147: - [Become a partner](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/overview)
148: - [View WhatsApp API OpenAPI Specification](https://github.com/meta/openapi)

1: # Pricing on the WhatsApp Business Platform
2: **Warning:** This page encompasses pricing across Cloud API and the Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp, for the following message categories: Marketing, utility, authentication, service, and Meta Business Agent.
3: **Warning:** This page reflects pricing updates that became effective as of October 1, 2026 by Messaging account timezone. Full detail on these updates is [below](#effective-october-1-2026).
4: ## How Meta charges for messages {#how-meta-charges-for-messages}
5: Effective July 1, 2025 – Meta charges on a **per-message basis**, aligned to industry standards. Meta charges by category–market, and only for messages from businesses to users. Meta does **not** charge for messages from users to businesses.
6: - Businesses are only charged when a message is _delivered_. Meta does _not_ charge for messages sent.
7: - Rates for messages vary based on 2 factors: a. the message [category](#message-categories) (“category”) and b. the recipient WhatsApp phone number’s [country calling code](#pricing-regions-on-the-rate-card-country-calling-codes) (“market”).
8: ### Message categories {#message-categories}
9: Meta has 5 different message categories on the WhatsApp Business Platform, with the introduction of Meta Business Agent as of July 1, 2026. A message from a business to a user only has 1 of the 5 categories and thus can only incur up to 1 charge, per the message’s category.
10: #### Template messages {#template-messages}
11: _Businesses can use template messages to reach out to users_ – **Template messages** (`"type":"template"`) can be delivered at any time. Template messages are categorized into 3 categories, per below; see [template categorization](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/template-categorization) to learn how template message categorization works.
12: 1. **Marketing** – template messages for promotional objectives
13: 2. **Utility** – template messages for transactional or informational objectives
14: 3. **Authentication** – template messages for identity verification objectives
15: #### Non-template messages {#non-template-messages}
16: _Businesses can use non-template messages only to respond to users_ – **Non-template messages** (`"type":"text"`, `"type":"image"`, and so on) can only be sent in an open 24-hour [customer service window](#customer-service-window-csw), which opens and resets with each user message. Note that a business can also choose to use template messages to respond to users; however, non-template messages _cannot_ be used to reach out to users.
17: 1. **Service** – Any non-template message _not_ powered by the Meta Business Agent Platform. These can be powered by a 3rd-party AI solution or people (like customer service representatives). Message types (outlined in [Send messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#message-types)) include address messages, audio messages, interactive location request messages, and more.
18: 2. **Meta Business Agent** – Any non-template message powered by the Meta Business Agent Platform.
19: ### Charges by message category {#charges-by-message-category}
20: #### Charges for marketing, utility, authentication and service messages {#charges-for-marketing-utility-authentication-and-service-messages}
21: - _Charge for_: Delivered message.
22: - _Meter_: Per message.
23: - _Rate_: Varies by market, aligned to industry standards. Rates by category vary as well, thus rates vary by market–category.
24: - _Cost per message_:
25: - Utility, authentication, and service: Fixed, per published rates.
26: - Marketing: For Cloud API, fixed, per published rates. For Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp, can vary per message if businesses choose to use the [max price feature](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/marketing-messages/pricing).
27: - _Volume tiers_: For utility and authentication messages only. Learn more about [volume tiers](#volume-tiers-for-utility-and-authentication-messages).
28: - _Frequency of updates_: Per published pricing calendar.
29: - _Free messages_: Two instances (all messages in free entry point window; free tier of monthly service messages). Learn more about [when Meta does not charge](#when-meta-does-not-charge).
30: #### Charges for Meta Business Agent messages {#charges-for-meta-business-agent-messages}
31: - _Charge for_: Delivered message.
32: - _Meter_: Per message, based on one per-token charge that encompasses AI agent processing (token consumption) and message delivery. Meta only charges for input and output tokens and does _not_ charge for cache tokens.
33: - _Rate_: One global rate of $2.00 USD per 1 million (M) tokens. One message typically consumes 20,000–25,000 tokens, which translates to approximately 4–5 cents (USD) per message.
34: - _Cost per message_: Varies with complexity. Simple responses consume fewer tokens and cost less; complex responses consume more tokens and cost more.
35: - _Volume tiers_: Do not apply.
36: - _Free messages_: Do not apply.
37: ### Pricing example {#example-across-all-message-categories}
38: Below is an example of an interaction between a business and a user. It starts with the business reaching out with a marketing template; using Meta Business Agent to respond to user questions; triggering an escalation to a customer service representative; and ultimately sending an order confirmation, all within one hour. Things to note:
39: - Meta charges for each message from the business to the user. Since there are 5 delivered messages, there are 5 charges.
40: - Every message has only one charge, per the category of that message. The “message category” and “charges incurred” columns always align.
41: - If this had all started with a user messaging a business from an Ad that Clicks to WhatsApp – thus happening in a [free entry point window](#free-entry-point-window-fep) – 3 of the 5 messages would _not_ be charged. Meta Business Agent remains charged.
42: | **Message content** | **Sender** | **Message type** | **Message category** | **Charges incurred** |
43: | Cart abandonment reminder | Business | Template | Marketing | Marketing |
44: | “Do you have this in a size Small?” | User | – | – | – |
45: | Meta-powered response to user’s question | Business | Non-template | Meta Business Agent | Meta Business Agent |
46: | “Do you have this in white?” | User | – | – | – |
47: | Meta-powered response to user’s question | Business | Non-template | Meta Business Agent | Meta Business Agent |
48: | “I’m ready to check-out, but my card is expired” | User | – | – | – |
49: | _Meta Business Agent hands off to customer service representative_ | _Meta Business Agent hands off to customer service representative_ | _Meta Business Agent hands off to customer service representative_ | _Meta Business Agent hands off to customer service representative_ | – |
50: | Customer service rep responds to user’s question | Business | Non-template | Service | Service |
51: | Order confirmation | Business | Template | Utility | Utility |
52: | | | | **Total charges** | **5 charges** |
53: ### Markets {#markets}
54: As of October 1, 2026 – Meta has 47 markets on its rate card. 39 of these represent named countries (like Brazil, Mexico, India) and 8 of these represent regions (like Rest of Latin America). A mapping of these with phone number country calling codes is [below](#pricing-regions-on-the-rate-card-country-calling-codes). If a business delivers a message to a user in a country that is…
55: - Named on the rate card → Meta charges that market’s rate
56: - In a “Rest of” region → Meta charges that region’s rate, across all markets within that region
57: ## What Meta charges for messages {#what-meta-charges-for-messages}
58: Meta publishes rates for transparency, across all 5 categories x 47 markets. See our [rate cards and volume tiers](#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers).
59: ### Rate cards and volume tiers {#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers}
60: Rate cards below reflect our current rates and volume tiers, effective October 1, 2026, based on your Messaging account timezone. Rates are also available interactively on our [WhatsApp Business website](https://business.whatsapp.com/products/platform-pricing#rates).

79: ### Currencies {#currencies}
80: As of July 1, 2026 – Meta has 16 currencies enabled on the WhatsApp Business Platform, after having introduced +10 currencies in 2026, as outlined in the table above. Currency selection is part of the Messaging account creation process; once selected, a currency cannot be changed. Businesses can leverage our [Currency Migration APIs](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/change-billing-currency) to more easily choose a different currency.
81: ### Comparing Meta Business Agent to service messages {#comparing-meta-business-agent-to-service-messages}
82: Below is a side-by-side comparison of the expected cost to send 10,000 AI-powered messages in response to users in Brazil via high-complexity AI models vs. Meta Business Agent. Estimates for 3rd-party AI solutions are based on publicly-available information and benchmarks.
83: | Message category | Service | Meta Business Agent |
84: | --- | --- | --- |
85: | **AI agent performance** | Higher-complexity | Higher-complexity |
86: | **AI agent cost** | **~9 ¢** per message<br>(estimate of 3rd-party cost) | **~4-5 ¢** per message<br>$2.00/1M tokens<br>x ~25k tokens<br>(estimate) |
87: | **Message delivery**1 | **0.68 ¢** per message1 | **~4-5 ¢** per message<br>$2.00/1M tokens<br>x ~25k tokens<br>(estimate) |
88: | **Total** | **~9-10 ¢** per message | **~4-5 ¢** per message |
89: | **Total for 10k messages** | **~ $968** | **~ $400 - $500** |
90: | 1 Based on Meta’s [current rate](#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers) for utility and authentication messages to users in Brazil. | 1 Based on Meta’s [current rate](#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers) for utility and authentication messages to users in Brazil. | 1 Based on Meta’s [current rate](#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers) for utility and authentication messages to users in Brazil. |
91: Also, price per-message for Meta Business Agent can vary by complexity, aligned to industry norms. The following table shows example interactions powered by Meta Business Agent and their estimated cost.
92: | **Type of interaction** | **Example user message** | **# messages to the user in the interaction** | **Tokens consumed** | **Est. Meta Business Agent cost** |
93: | _Simple inquiry_ | “At what time do you open?” | 4 | ~80k → ~20k/mssg | ~ 16-20 ¢ |
94: | _Complex interaction_ | "I'm stuck on step 3 of this assembly — can you walk me through it?" | 10 | ~250k → ~25k/mssg | ~ 40 - 50 ¢ |
95: ## When Meta may update pricing {#when-meta-may-update-pricing}
96: ### Pricing calendar {#pricing-calendar}
97: As of September 2025, Meta has published a pricing calendar to provide clear, go-forward guidance to better enable businesses to plan and prepare for pricing updates:
98: - Meta may update pricing only on the 1st day of each quarter, thus up to 4 times per year: January 1, April 1, July 1, and/or October 1.
99: - Meta will provide advanced notice that is better aligned to the effort required to implement different types of pricing updates, per below:
100: | **Type of pricing update** | **Examples** | **Minimum advanced notice** |
101: | **Rate card update** | Updating the rate for a given market–category<br>Updating the volume tiers for a given market–category (utility and authentication only)<br>Moving a market from one [pricing region](#pricing-regions-on-the-rate-card-country-calling-codes) (for example, “Other”) to another OR to be standalone on the rate card | 1 month |
102: | **Pricing model add-on** | Our July 1, 2025, introduction of new [volume tiers](#volume-tiers-for-utility-and-authentication-messages) for utility and authentication messages | 3 months |
103: | **Pricing model change** | Our July 1, 2025 update to our pricing model, from conversation-based pricing to per-message pricing | 6 months |
104: ## When Meta does _not_ charge {#when-meta-does-not-charge}
105: There are two instances where Meta does _not_ charge for a message a business delivers to a WhatsApp user:
106: - _In the_ [free entry point window](#free-entry-point-window-fep) – In this window, Meta does _not_ charge for marketing, utility, authentication or service messages. Meta Business Agent messages remain charged.
107: - _For the_ [first 1,000 service messages each month](#free-tier-of-monthly-service-messages) – For each business phone number, Meta provides 1,000 free service messages per month, which do not roll over but reset monthly. Thus, Meta only charges as of the 1,001st service message for each business phone number.
108: Also, as noted above, Meta does not charge for messages from a WhatsApp user to a business.
109: ## Ways Meta provides value via pricing {#ways-meta-provides-value-via-pricing}
110: ### Free entry point window (FEP) {#free-entry-point-window-fep}
111: If a WhatsApp user messages you via an ad that clicks to WhatsApp (CTWA) using a device running our Android or iOS app (since our desktop and web apps are not supported):
112: 1. A [customer service window](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#customer-service-windows) is opened.
113: 2. If you respond within the [customer service window](#customer-service-window-csw) with a marketing, utility, authentication or service message:
114: - That message is _not_ charged and opens a Free Entry Point (“FEP”) window, starting from the time when you responded.
115: - The FEP window may remain open for up to 7 days.
116: - While open, Meta does _not_ charge for marketing, utility, authentication or service messages. Meta continues to charge for Meta Business Agent messages in the FEP window.
117: In the example below, all messages from the business to the user are _not_ charged because they opened or were in the FEP window.
118: | **Message content** | **Sender** | **Message type** | **Message category** | **Charges incurred** |
119: | User messages from a CTWA ad:<br>“Do you have this in white?” | User | – | – | – |
120: | [Interactive media carousel message](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/interactive-media-carousel-messages/) to showcase available colors for that product | Business | Template | Marketing | _No charge_<br>_Opens FEP window_ |
121: | “Do you have this in size small?” | User | – | – | – |
122: | Customer service rep responds to user’s question | Business | Non-template | Service | _No charge_ in open FEP window |
123: | Order confirmation | Business | Template | Utility | _No charge in open FEP window_ |
124: | | | | **Total charges** | **0 charges** |
125: #### Free entry point windows with multiple Messaging accounts {#free-entry-point-windows-with-multiple-messaging-accounts}
126: Like customer service windows, a free entry point window is tracked for the business and WhatsApp user pair, not for an individual Messaging account. When several Messaging accounts send on the same business phone number, they all share the same FEP window:
127: - Any Messaging account sending on that phone number can send free messages while the FEP window is open.
128: - The Messaging account that funded the Click to WhatsApp ad does not get exclusive use of the window.
129: - If a different Messaging account responds to the WhatsApp user than the one that funded the ad, messages are still free while the window is open.
130: ### Free tier of monthly service messages {#free-tier-of-monthly-service-messages}
131: **Warning:** This only applies to service messages, as of 12am by Messaging account timezone on October 1, 2026.
132: As Meta resumes charging for service messages, Meta provides every business phone number with a free tier of 1,000 service messages per month.
133: - Each business phone number has one free tier of 1,000 delivered service messages per month. Meta charges as of the 1,001st service message per month, after the free tier has been used.
134: - Unused service messages in the free tier do not roll over to the next month. The free tier resets monthly for each business phone number (for example, 1,000 for October with no roll-over; 1,000 for November with no roll-over). This reset happens at 12am by Messaging account timezone.
135: - If businesses do not have a payment method for their Messaging account(s), Meta will deliver service messages within the free tier but _not_ deliver them after the free tier has been used. To ensure continuity of service messages as of October 1, 2026, please ensure you have a payment method in [Billing Hub](https://business.facebook.com/latest/billing_hub/).
136: Status [messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status) webhooks for service messages delivered within the free tier include a `subtype` field set to `free_tier` in the pricing object.
137: When Meta begins to charge – as of the 1,001st service message each month – the pricing type (`<PRICING_TYPE>`) in the pricing object of status [messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status) webhooks for messages with a pricing category (`<PRICING_CATEGORY>`) of service will change from `free_customer_service` to `regular` as outlined below:
138: | Which service messages | Through Sep. 30, 2026 | Through Sep. 30, 2026 | As of Oct. 1, 2026 | As of Oct. 1, 2026 | `type` | Charged | `type` | Charged |
139: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
140: | Service messages in the free tier, per business phone number | `free_customer_service` | **No** | `free_customer_service` | **No** |
141: | Service messages after the free tier has been used, per business phone number | `free_customer_service` | **No** | `regular` | **Yes** |
142: **Service message in the free monthly tier** – For a service message delivered while the business phone number is within its free tier:
143: ```json
144: "pricing": {
145: "billable": false,
146: "pricing_model": "PMP",
147: "type": "free_customer_service",
148: "category": "service",
149: "subtype": "free_tier"
150: }
151: ```
152: **Service message that is charged** – For a service message delivered _after_ the business phone number’s free tier has been used:
153: ```json
154: "pricing": {
155: "billable": true,
156: "pricing_model": "PMP",
157: "type": "regular",
158: "category": "service"
159: }
160: ```
161: ### Volume tiers for utility and authentication messages {#volume-tiers-for-utility-and-authentication-messages}
162: **Warning:** Volume tiers only apply to utility and authentication messages.
163: Businesses can unlock lower utility and authentication rates based on the number of messages they send in a month, by market–category.
164: #### Tiering accrual {#tiering-accrual}
165: - Messages are aggregated at the business portfolio level, across all Messaging accounts owned by the portfolio — To determine what tier rates may apply in a given month for a given market–category pair, Meta aggregates messages across all of a business portfolio's Messaging accounts for each market-category pair (for example, Brazil–authentication, Brazil–utility, India–authentication, and so on).
166: - Only messages that are charged count toward the tiers. Thus, any utility or authentication messages sent in a free entry point window do _not_ count toward volume tiers.
167: - Volume tiers will be determined solely by Meta — All insights data is approximate due to small variations in data processing. Undue reliance should not be placed on insights data.
168: #### How volume tiers work {#how-volume-tiers-work}
169: - Tiers are market–category specific — Volume tiers are aligned to our rate cards and differ by market (for example, Brazil or Rest of Latin America) and category (utility, authentication).
170: - Rates are tier-specific — When a business sends enough messages at a given market–category pair to reach the next tier, they unlock the rate of the next tier, specifically for messages in that tier. This rate applies across all of their Messaging accounts.
171: - Tiers reset monthly — At the start of the next month (12am Messaging account timezone), message count resets to 0 and businesses begin to accrue messages toward that month.
172: #### Volume tier examples {#volume-tier-examples}
173: The table below is illustrative and only highlights the dynamics of volume tiers. Please refer to our [rate cards](#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers) to see the rates charged.
174: | **India x Authentication messages** (specific market x message category) | **India x Authentication messages** (specific market x message category) | **India x Authentication messages** (specific market x message category) | **India x Authentication messages** (specific market x message category) | **India x Authentication messages** (specific market x message category) |
175: | **Messages per month** | **Messages per month** | **What Meta charges** (illustrative) | **What Meta charges** (illustrative) | **How it works** |
176: | **From** | **To** | **Rate** | **vs. List rate** | **How it works** |
177: | 0 | A | List rate | 0% | First A messages are charged list rate |
178: | A + 1 | B | Tier rate 1 | – 5% | Only messages A+1 to B are charged tier Rate 1 |
179: | B + 1 | C | Tier rate 2 | – 10% | Only messages B+1 to C are charged tier Rate 2 |
180: | C + 1 | ∞ | Tier rate 3 | – 15% | Only messages C+1 onward are charged tier rate 3 |
181: Below are several examples to highlight how the tiers work and what is charged in a given month, for a given market–category. These examples refer to the illustrative table above:
182: - _Example 1: A business that sends a total of B authentication messages in a month to India is charged:_
183: - List rate for the first A messages.
184: - Tier rate 1 for messages A+1 to B.
185: - Total charges for that month = Rate per tier 𝗑 messages in each tier.
186: - _Example 2: A business that starts to be charged our authentication-international rates on the 15th day of the month:_
187: - Day 1 to 14 of that month: Volume tiers apply on the authentication rate.
188: - Day 15 onward of that month: Volume tiers apply on the authentication-international rate, with messages continuing to accrue in that month. For example, if a business has already reached the Tier 2, the business would be charged Tier 2’s authentication-international rate.
189: - _Example 3: A business has 3 Messaging accounts sending authentication messages to India. For Messaging account A, it is still July 31 based on their timezone. For Messaging accounts B and C, it is already August 1 based on their timezone. For July, the business is already being charged Tier Rate 1._
190: - The business portfolio will be accruing toward tiers for both July (via Messaging account A) and August (via Messaging accounts B, C) for a period of time.
191: - The business can reach the next tier for July, via Messaging account A. If that happens, messages for the remainder of July for Messaging account A will be charged Tier Rate 2.
192: - _Example 4: A business has 3 Messaging accounts, integrated across 2 partners. Provider 1 sends the first B messages in a given month, and provider 2 starts sending messages as of when the business is in the 3rd tier. The business does not send enough messages that month to reach the next tier. What Meta charges each provider:_
193: - Provider 1: List rate for A messages, then Tier Rate 1 from A+1 to B, and Tier Rate 2 for B+1 to C.
194: - Provider 2: Tier Rate 2 across all of their messages.
195: #### Tiering webhooks {#tiering-webhooks}
196: Starting October 1, 2025, an [`account_update`](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/account_update) webhook with `event` set to `VOLUME_BASED_PRICING_TIER_UPDATE` will be triggered when your Messaging account reaches a new volume tier, in any market, in a given month. This complements our [`pricing_analytics`](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/analytics#pricing-analytics) endpoint, which will continue to provide intra-month tiering progress and tiering information for delivered messages.
197: Example webhook:
198: ```json
199: {
200: "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
201: "entry": [
202: {
203: "id": "102290129340398",
204: "time": 1743451903,
205: "changes": [
206: {
207: "value": {
208: "volume_tier_info": {
209: "tier_update_time": 1743451903,
210: "pricing_category": "UTILITY",
211: "tier": "25000001:50000000",
212: "effective_month": "2025-11",
213: "region": "India"
214: },
215: "event": "VOLUME_BASED_PRICING_TIER_UPDATE"
216: },
217: "field": "account_update"
218: }
219: ]
220: }
221: ]
222: }
223: ```
224: - `tier_update_time` tells when your Messaging account reached a higher volume tier (Unix timestamp).
225: - `pricing_category` tells you the template category (`UTILITY` or `AUTHENTICATION`) for which your new volume tier rate applies.
226: - `tier` tells you the new volume tier's lower and upper bounds.
227: - `effective_month` tells you the month in which your new volume tier rate is in effect.
228: - `region` tells you the WhatsApp user country/region for which your new volume tier rate applies.
229: Note it’s possible for multiple [`account_update`](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/account_update) webhooks to be triggered that describe the same tier switch event. In these cases, use the webhook with the smaller `tier_update_time` Unix timestamp as the official webhook.

232: ## Other pricing mechanics {#other-pricing-mechanics}
233: ### Customer service window (CSW) {#customer-service-window-csw}
234: When a WhatsApp user messages you or [calls you](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/calling/pricing#how-calling-changes-the-24-hour-customer-service-window), a 24-hour timer called a _customer service window_ starts. If the user messages or calls you again before the timer expires, the timer resets to 24 hours. Businesses can only send non-template messages to users when this window is open. If it is not open, businesses can only send template messages to reach out to users.
235: As a reminder, you can only send messages to WhatsApp users who have opted in to receiving messages from you. Learn more about [customer service windows](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/messages/send-messages#customer-service-windows).
236: ### Authentication-international rates {#authentication-international-rates}
237: Specific markets have an authentication-international rate. Our [rate cards](#rate-cards-and-volume-tiers) reflect these rates, for the markets where they apply. See [Authentication-International rates](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/authentication-international-rates) to learn about these rates and if they apply to your business.

528: - Effective April 1, 2025 – Lowered [authentication-international conversation rates](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/authentication-international-rates) for Egypt, Nigeria, Pakistan, and South Africa.
529: - Effective February 1, 2025 – Lowered [authentication conversation rates](#what-meta-charges-for-messages) for Egypt, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates.
530: - Effective November 1, 2024 – [Service conversations](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/conversation-based-pricing#service-conversations) are now free for all businesses.
531: - Effective October 1, 2024 – Updated [marketing conversation rates](#what-meta-charges-for-messages) in India, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom.
532: - Effective August 1, 2024 – Lowered [utility conversation rates](#what-meta-charges-for-messages).
533: ## Other pricing topics {#other-pricing-topics}
534: ### Marketing – Max-price feature for Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp {#marketing-max-price-feature-for-marketing-messages-api-for-whatsapp}
535: Starting in 2026, businesses integrated into Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp can choose to set a [max-price](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/marketing-messages/pricing) per marketing message delivery; when a max-price is set, Meta will charge that max-price or lower for delivery.
536: ### Service – Pricing policy for AI Providers leveraging WhatsApp Business Platform {#service-pricing-policy-for-ai-providers-leveraging-whatsapp-business-platform}
537: See the [AI Providers pricing policy](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/ai-providers), effective February 16, 2026 and updated as of May 12, 2026. Pricing updates for service messages launching October 1, 2026 do not apply to AI Providers; see the [AI Providers pricing policy](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/ai-providers) for how Meta charges them for service messages.
538: ### Service - Pricing policy for eligible governments and non-profits using the WhatsApp Business Platform {#service-pricing-policy-for-eligible-governments-and-non-profits}
539: Starting October 1, 2026 - Service messages remain free beyond the monthly free tier only for eligible government and non-profit organizations using the WhatsApp Business Platform. This pricing policy will be in effect through December 31, 2027.
540: Meta continues to support governments and non-profit organizations, and this policy allows Meta to enable eligible governments and non-profits to maintain an always-on presence on WhatsApp, to respond to and engage with WhatsApp users.
541: Eligible organizations include:
542: - Government departments and agencies; inter-governmental organizations
543: - Community non-profit organizations, including those in public health, crisis response, disaster relief and non-partisan civic engagement
544: For organizations Meta has identified as eligible, this policy will apply as of 12am by Messaging account timezone on October 1, 2026.
545: #### Understand if you are eligible {#understand-if-you-are-eligible}
546: There are two ways for Solution Providers and businesses to understand eligibility for this policy:
547: - As of October 12, 2026, via webhooks. Ingest the `paid_exempt` value of the new `subtype` field to build a view of which Messaging accounts are eligible.
548: - As of October 23, 2026, via the `service_pricing_policy` field. This scales better: you can query any or all of the Messaging accounts you manage, and Meta confirms which are eligible.
549: **New `subtype` field in webhooks**
550: Status [messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status) webhooks include a new `subtype` field in the pricing object. Service messages that are free because the organization is eligible for this policy have `subtype` set to `paid_exempt`. Service messages that are free because they were delivered within the business phone number's [free tier](#free-tier-of-monthly-service-messages) have `subtype` set to `free_tier` instead, so only `paid_exempt` indicates eligibility.
551: Example pricing object in a [status messages webhook](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status), for a service message from an eligible government or non-profit organization:
552: ```json
553: {
554: "pricing": {
555: "billable": false,
556: "pricing_model": "PMP",
557: "category": "service",
558: "type": "free_customer_service",
559: "subtype": "paid_exempt"
560: }
561: }
562: ```
563: - `type` is `free_customer_service`, or `free_group_customer_service` for group messages.
564: - `subtype` is `paid_exempt` when the service message is free because the organization is eligible for this policy.
565: - `subtype` is `free_tier` when the service message is free because it was delivered within the business phone number's monthly free tier. It does not indicate eligibility.
566: **New `service_pricing_policy` field on accounts**
567: To check whether a Messaging account is eligible:
568: ```html
569: GET /<WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID>?fields=id,name,service_pricing_policy
570: ```
571: Get the value for Messaging accounts your business portfolio owns or manages on behalf of your clients:
572: ```html
573: GET /<BUSINESS_PORTFOLIO_ID>/owned_whatsapp_business_accounts?fields=id,name,service_pricing_policy
574: GET /<BUSINESS_PORTFOLIO_ID>/client_whatsapp_business_accounts?fields=id,name,service_pricing_policy
575: ```
576: Based on the results, you can understand which Messaging accounts are eligible:
577: - **Eligible** if `service_pricing_policy` is `PAID_EXEMPT`. Service messages from this Messaging account are free under this policy.
578: - **Not eligible** if `service_pricing_policy` is `REGULAR`. These Messaging accounts would be charged at [published rates](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing#what-meta-charges-for-messages) for service messages as of October 1, 2026, and still benefit from the [free monthly tier of service messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing#free-tier-of-monthly-service-messages).
579: #### Request a review of eligibility {#request-a-review-of-eligibility}
580: Meta is also building a way for Solution Providers and businesses to request a review of their eligibility for this policy, and will provide an update once it is available.
581: ### Calling – WhatsApp Business Calling API pricing {#calling-whatsapp-business-calling-api-pricing}
582: The WhatsApp Business Calling API has different pricing. See our [Calling API pricing document](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/calling/pricing) to learn more.
583: ### Conversation-based pricing {#conversation-based-pricing}
584: [Conversation-based pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/conversation-based-pricing) is deprecated. It was replaced with per-message pricing on July 1, 2025.
585: ## Analytics {#analytics}
586: Use the [`pricing_analytics` field](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/analytics#pricing-analytics) to get per-message pricing breakdowns and tiering information for delivered messages.
587: ## Pricing webhooks {#pricing-webhooks}
588: Billable messages have `type` set to `regular` in the pricing object of status [messages](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status) webhooks:
589: ```json
590: "pricing": {
591: "billable": true,
592: "pricing_model": "PMP",
593: "type": "regular",
594: "category": "<PRICING_CATEGORY>"
595: }
596: ```
597: The `<PRICING_CATEGORY>` tells you what rate was applied (for example, marketing). See the status messages webhook reference for a list of possible values.
598: Note that currently, tiering information is not included in any webhooks. Use the [`pricing_analytics` field](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/analytics#pricing-analytics) to get tiering information for delivered messages.
599: ## Billing {#billing}
600: Billing and billing-related actions are handled through the Meta Business Suite. See [About Billing For Your WhatsApp Business Account](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2225184664363779) for more information.
601: ### Billing attribution with multiple Messaging accounts {#billing-attribution-with-multiple-messaging-accounts}
602: When several Messaging accounts send on the same business phone number, charges are attributed to the specific Messaging account that sent each message. The `messaging_account_id` — passed on the send message API call, or resolved from your app token — determines which Messaging account is billed for a given template message delivery.
603: - Each Messaging account maintains its own billing relationship, payment method, and spend limits, regardless of how many other Messaging accounts send on the same phone number.
604: - Volume tiers are calculated at the business portfolio level across all Messaging accounts the portfolio owns, not per phone number.
605: - Solution Providers are charged only for messages sent through their own Messaging account. Messages sent by other partners on the same phone number do not appear on their invoice.
606: ---
607: Full documentation index for this product: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/llms.txt

354: REST API
355: Aircall Public API is a classic REST API. It can be used with any programming languages and offers a fast, reliable and secure access to an Aircall account information.
356: The root endpoint of Aircall Public API is https://api.aircall.io/v1.
357: Please note that only HTTPS requests are valid as requests will communicate over SSL connection.
358: Each Public API request must be authenticated and should not exceed the rate limit, please check the Authentication and the rate limiting sections before jumping in our documentation!
359: Request
360: GET https://api.aircall.io
361: Response
362: {
363: "resource": "Aircall Documentation",
364: "contact": "support@aircall.io"
365: }
366: Authentication
367: Introduction
368: With Aircall Public API, Authentication can be done through OAuth or Basic Auth.
369: If you want to build an App for companies using Aircall - this is mainly the case for Technology Partners - please use the OAuth flow. It is a requirement to be listed on the Aircall App Marketplace. You can create a partner-specific account by signing up here!
370: If you are an Aircall customer, building for your own Aircall account only, the Basic Auth flow will do the trick.
371: All endpoints behave similarly between the two authentication methods, unless indicated otherwise in the documentation.
372: OAuth ﹣ Technology Partners
373: Aircall built a powerful Ecosystem of apps, providing its customers an easy way to enhance their voice experience.
374: In Aircall, integrations are enabled at the Company level, which means they can only be set by an Admin user. It is possible to configure several instances of an integration on one Aircall account.
375: Aircall implemented the OAuth 2.0 authentication protocol so you can easily build an app on top of Aircall and deploy it on Aircall's Marketplace.
376: Beyond the added security and scalability, the Aircall OAuth flow will make your app visible to all customers in the Aircall Dashboard and provide a simple way for customers to install your app from Aircall or from your own website.
377: Want to know every secret about OAuth? Read the official documentation RFC 6750!
378: Oauth terminology
379: install_uri
380: String
381: Aircall fetches the install_uri URI when starting the OAuth flow. This step is often used to display a Settings page, instructions on how to use the app or any useful information for the Admin.
382: It must eventually forward to https://dashboard.aircall.io/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and scope=public_api query params. See Step 3 of the OAuth flow.
383: Must use HTTPS.
384: redirect_uri
385: String
386: Aircall sends the Admin's authorization code to the redirect_uri URI, once they authorized the app, or the error if any.
387: Must use HTTPS.
388: client_id
389: String
390: Used in both the [DASHBOARD] /oauth/authorize and [API] /v1/oauth/token request.
391: Provided by Aircall.
392: client_secret
393: String
394: Used in the request body of [API] /v1/oauth/token.
395: Provided by Aircall.
396: code
397: String
398: An authentication code provided by Aircall valid for 10min.
399: Must be converted in an access_token (see this endpoint).
400: access_token
401: String
402: Token used to send requests to Aircall Public API as a Company.
403: More info on how to use it here.
404: state
405: String
406: An optional string value created by your app to maintain state between the request and callback. This parameter should be used for preventing Cross-site Request Forgery and will be passed back to you, unchanged, in your redirect_uri.
407: OAuth credentials
408: Before starting building the OAuth flow for your app, you will need to get OAuth client_id and client_secret from Aircall. Click the start building button on top of the page and fill in the form. We will get back to you shortly.
409: When signing up, an install_uri and a redirect_uri will be asked, make sure you have them ready. Read the OAuth flow first to understand what they are!
410: OAuth flow
411: Aircall ﹣ When an Admin installs an App, a popup opens up and loads the install_uri URL.
412: Partner ﹣ A Web server receives the GET request on the install_uri route. This step is often used to display a custom Settings page, instructions on how to use the app and/or any useful information for the Admin.
413: Partner ﹣ Once Step 2 is done, Web server redirects/forwards the request to the following Aircall URL:
414: https://dashboard.aircall.io/oauth/authorize?client_id=XX&redirect_uri=YY&response_type=code&scope=public_api&state=ZZ
415: Aircall ﹣ Aircall then displays the authorization window. Only users who are Admins will be able to see this window, others will be redirected to the Download page. Once the Admin consented to the permissions the app is requesting (scope=public_api), Aircall loads the redirect_uri URL with a code parameter.
416: Partner ﹣ Web server receives the GET request on the redirect_uri route with the code query param…
417: Partner ﹣ …and sends a [POST] https://api.aircall.io/v1/oauth/token request to Aircall's Public API with the proper body params (see here).
418: Aircall ﹣ Aircall authenticates the [POST] request, create an access_token and sends it back to the Web server.
419: Partner ﹣ Web server stores the access_token for further use!
420: Start the instructions at Step 3 if you want to trigger the install flow directly from your interface and not from the Aircall Dashboard.
421: Integrations can only be installed by users who are Admins on Aircall!
422: Check out our Ruby example app on Github to better understand how to implement the Aircall OAuth flow!
423: Get an access_token via the Public API
424: Once you get an OAuth authorization code from the OAuth flow, you need to convert it into a Public API access_token with the following request.
425: This access_token will then be used as a Bearer token in the Authorization header of each Public API requests you will make and does not expire.
426: Body params
427: client_id
428: String
429: The client_id provided by Aircall. More information in the Oauth credentials section.
430: Mandatory field.
431: client_secret
432: String
433: The client_secret provided by Aircall. More information in the Oauth credentials section.
434: Mandatory field.
435: code
436: String
437: The OAuth authorization code Aircall sent back to your server.
438: Mandatory field.
439: redirect_uri
440: String
441: Your redirect_uri.
442: Mandatory field.
443: grant_type
444: String
445: Must be authorization_code.
446: Mandatory field.
447: Request
448: POST https://api.aircall.io/v1/oauth/token
449: {
450: "client_id": YOUR_AIRCALL_CLIENT_ID,
451: "client_secret": YOUR_AIRCALL_CLIENT_SECRET,
452: "code": TMP_AUTHORIZATION_CODE,
453: "redirect_uri": YOUR_REDIRECT_URI,
454: "grant_type": "authorization_code"
455: }
456: Response
457: Status: 200 OK
458: {
459: "access_token": "2d492d492d492d492d492d492d492d",
460: "token_type": "Bearer",
461: "created_at": 1585868617
462: }
463: Test the access_token
464: A /v1/ping endpoint is available to test the access_token retrieved via the Public API (as described here).
465: The access_token must be used in the Authorization HTTP header of your request, as a Bearer token.
466: Request
467: curl -X GET https://api.aircall.io/v1/ping \
468: -H "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN}"
469: Response
470: Status: 200 OK
471: {
472: "ping": "pong"
473: }
474: Basic Auth ﹣ Aircall customers
475: As an Aircall customer, an api_id and api_token are needed to use Aircall Public API: go to your Company's Settings page. In the API Keys section, click on Add a new API key and get your api_token and api_token.
476: Do not forget to copy/paste your api_token somewhere safe, we won't be able to retrieve it for you as Aircall does not store it in plain text!
477: If you are building an App for several companies using Aircall, please refer to the OAuth section.
478: Public API requests must be authenticated using HTTP Basic Authentication. The api_id is the username and the api_token is the password for each Public API requests.
479: The Authorization HTTP header is constructed as follows:
480: The api_id and api_token are concatenated with a single colon :.
481: The resulting string is encoded using Base64.
482: The authorization header results in Authorization: Basic YOUR_ENCODED_STRING.
483: Always prefer Base64 encoding in the Authorization HTTP header rather than the following: https://api_id:api_token@api.aircall.io.
484: It is not recommended to authenticate requests passing the api_id and api_token in the URL for security reasons and as some programming languages and platforms do not support it!
485: Request
486: curl -X GET https://api.aircall.io/v1/ping \
487: -H "Authorization: Basic {YOUR_ENCODED_STRING}"
488: Response
489: Status: 200 OK
490: {
491: "ping": "pong"
492: }
493: Rate limiting
494: Aircall limits the number of requests to its Public API to 120 requests per minute per company. The following headers are available in API headers' responses when the rate limit has been reached, giving more insight on your API usage:
495: header
496: description
497: X-AircallApi-Limit
498: Limit of requests for the API key used.
499: X-AircallApi-Remaining
500: Remaining requests for this API key.
501: X-AircallApi-Reset
502: Timestamp when the counter will be reset.
503: Contact us on support.aircall.io if you need to make more requests per minute, we will add a higher rate limit to your API keys!
504: Pagination
505: When retrieving a list of objects with a [GET] request, results are being paginated by Aircall.
506: Pagination information will be presented in the meta object, available in the payload body and described below.
507: The meta object
508: count
509: Integer
510: Count of items present in the current page.
511: total
512: Integer
513: Count of items in total, according to search params.
514: current_page
515: Integer
516: Current page number.
517: per_page
518: Integer
519: Number of results retrieved per page.
520: Default is 20. Minimum is 1, maximum is 50.
521: next_page_link
522: String
523: URL to follow to go to the next page results.
524: Can be null.
525: previous_page_link
526: String
527: URL to follow to go to the previous page results.
528: Can be null.
529: The two following attributes can be set in any URL query params to navigate from one page to the other:
530: Query params
531: page
532: Integer
533: Current page.
534: Default is 1.
535: per_page
536: Integer
537: Number of results retrieved per page
538: Default is 20.
539: Calls and Contacts are limited to 10,000 items, even with pagination on.
540: To pass over this limit, we encourage you to use the from param as much as you can!

553: Errors
554: Aircall uses standard HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request:
555: 2xx codes indicate success
556: 4xx codes indicate an error that failed given the information provided
557: 5xx codes indicate an error with Aircall's servers
558: Application error responses include an error title and a human-readable troubleshoot description. They also include message, an errors array, and success: false. Requests rejected at the API gateway before they reach an application, such as invalid credentials, can return a shorter gateway error.
559: The Conversation endpoints return only error and troubleshoot.
560: For Outbound Campaigns, message is the machine-readable code to use for specific handling. A recognised domain error uses a semantic code such as INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION or OUTCOME_IN_USE; otherwise it falls back to the HTTP status constant such as BAD_REQUEST or UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY. errors[].detail always keeps that status-level constant for broad HTTP categorisation. Internal shared-library codes, including numeric codes, are never exposed.
561: More detailed HTTP response codes are provided in each endpoint's documentation.
