606: Versioning
607: Versioning Strategy
608: Aircall APIs and Webhooks are versioned to allow for continuous evolution and improvement while maintaining backward compatibility for existing integrations. API versions are indicated in the URL path. The webhook event names are now suffixed with “v2”.
609: For APIs, Aircall uses URL-based versioning, where the API version is included directly in the endpoint path. For example:
610: Version 1 endpoints: /v1/users, /v1/calls, etc.
611: Version 2 endpoints: /v2/users, etc.
612: For Webhook events, the version number is suffixed in the event name. For example:
613: Version 1 webhook event: user.connected
614: Version 2 webhook event: user.connected.v2
615: As of now, v2 of user APIs and webhook events is available
616: Content-Type
617: Every POST, PUT and DELETE HTTP request sent to Aircall Public API must specify the Content-Type entity header to application/json.
618: Request
619: HTTP headers:
620: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }

1065: In this section, we list all the available Public APIs.
1066: User V1
1067: User overview
1068: Get all users associated to an Aircall account, or retrieve, create and update info about one specific User! You can also start outbound calls from a User's Aircall Workspace.
1069: Users can be either Admins or Agents:
1070: Admins: can access the Dashboard and Aircall Workspace, and can invite other users.
1071: Agents: can only access Aircall Workspace and recording files.
1072: Users are assigned to Numbers.
1073: Attributes
1074: id
1075: Integer
1076: Unique identifier for the User.
1077: direct_link
1078: String
1079: Direct API URL.
1080: name
1081: String
1082: Full name of the User.
1083: Results of first_name last_name.
1084: email
1085: String
1086: Email of the User.
1087: created_at
1088: String
1089: Timestamp when the User was created, in UTC.
1090: available
1091: Boolean
1092: Current availability status of the User, based on their working hours.
1093: availability_status
1094: String
1095: Current working status of the User.
1096: Can be available, custom (= available according to their Working Hours and Timezone) or unavailable (= Do Not Disturb or other unavailable status). More availablility statuses can be retrieved, see the Availability table below.
1097: substatus
1098: String
1099: Current substatus of the User.
1100: If user selects availability_status as available or custom (available according to working hours or timezone) then substatus will be always_open.
1101: If user selects availability_status as unavailable and doesn't select a substatus or unavailability reason in Aircall Workspace then it will be always_closed.
1102: If user selects availability_status as unavailable and selects a substatus or unavailability reason in Aircall Workspace i.e. Out for lunch, On a break, In training, Back office or Other. The substatus will contain the exact substauts or unavailability reason selected.
1103: numbers
1104: Array
1105: List of Numbers associated to this User.
1106: time_zone
1107: String
1108: The User's timezone. This can be set either from the Dashboard or Aircall Workspace (check our Knowledge Base).
1109: Default is Etc/UTC. More details on Timezones here.
1110: language
1111: String
1112: The User's preferred language. This can be set either from the Dashboard or Aircall Workspace (check our Knowledge Base).
1113: The format is IETF language tag. Default is en-US.
1114: wrap_up_time
1115: Integer
1116: A pre-set timer triggered after a call has ended, during which the user can’t receive any calls. Learn more..

1535: User V2
1536: User V2 overview
1537: Get all users associated to an Aircall account, or retrieve, create and update info about one specific User V2! You can also start outbound calls from a User V2's Aircall Workspace.
1538: Users can be either Admins or Agents:
1539: Admins: can access the Dashboard and Aircall Workspace, and can invite other users.
1540: Agents: can only access Aircall Workspace and recording files.
1541: Please note User v2 object doesn't include a numbers object
1542: Attributes
1543: id
1544: Integer
1545: Unique identifier for the User.
1546: direct_link
1547: String
1548: Direct API URL.
1549: name
1550: String
1551: Full name of the User.
1552: Results of first_name last_name.
1553: email
1554: String
1555: Email of the User.
1556: created_at
1557: String
1558: Timestamp when the User was created, in UTC.
1559: available
1560: Boolean
1561: Current availability status of the User, based on their working hours.
1562: availability_status
1563: String
1564: Current working status of the User.
1565: Can be available, custom (= available according to their Working Hours and Timezone) or unavailable (= Do Not Disturb or other unavailable status). More availablility statuses can be retrieved, see the Availability table below.
1566: substatus
1567: String
1568: Current substatus of the User.
1569: If user selects availability_status as available or custom (available according to working hours or timezone) then substatus will be always_open.
1570: If user selects availability_status as unavailable and doesn't select a substatus or unavailability reason in Aircall Workspace then it will be always_closed.
1571: If user selects availability_status as unavailable and selects a substatus or unavailability reason in Aircall Workspace i.e. Out for lunch, On a break, In training, Back office or Other. The substatus will contain the exact substauts or unavailability reason selected.
1572: time_zone
1573: String
1574: The User's timezone. This can be set either from the Dashboard or Aircall Workspace (check our Knowledge Base).
1575: Default is Etc/UTC. More details on Timezones here.
1576: language
1577: String
1578: The User's preferred language. This can be set either from the Dashboard or Aircall Workspace (check our Knowledge Base).
1579: The format is IETF language tag. Default is en-US.
1580: wrap_up_time
1581: Integer
1582: A pre-set timer triggered after a call has ended, during which the user can't receive any calls. Learn more..
1583: last_call_id
1584: Integer
1585: The unique identifier of the last call associated with the user's wrap-up time.
1586: This attribute is only available in user.wut_start.v2 and user.wut_end.v2 webhook events and not in User APIs.
1587: If mandatory call tagging is enabled in Aircall Workspace and wrap-up time is set to zero or any other duration, or if a call is transferred to an external number and does not connect, then last_call_id won't be available.
1588: Availability
1589: available
1590: String
1591: Agent ready to answer calls.
1592: offline
1593: String
1594: Agent not online.
1595: do_not_disturb
1596: String
1597: Agent toggled themself as do not disturb.
1598: in_call
1599: String
1600: Agent is currently on a call.
1601: after_call_work
1602: String
1603: Agent is performing their after-call work (tagging a call or wrapping up).

2168: Call
2169: Call overview
2170: Calls are an essential part of how Aircall users interact with the product. Our mission is to give real-time insights to make the call experience as delightful as possible!
2171: There are three types of calls:
2172: Inbound calls: where an external person reaches an Agent.
2173: Outbound calls: where an Agent starts a call from Aircall Workspace to reach an external person.
2174: Internal calls: where an Agent calls another Agent.
2175: More information available on each type of Call at the bottom of this section.
2176: Please refer to the User object if you are looking to start an outbound call or to dial a phone number!

2181: Please note, Call id Data Type is Int64

2304: 1. Inbound calls
2305: Inbound calls are initiated by an external person, calling an Aircall Number. Once started, calls will follow the Call distribution tree defined in the Aircall Dashboard (see our Knowledge Base).
2306: If an Inbound call is not answered, it is then considered as missed. All missed calls will have the missed_call_reason field defined in their payload, the answered_at field will be null, and the teams field will be empty ([]).
2307: The duration field is computed by the following: ended_at - started_at. As the ringing time is included in it, use the ended_at - answered_at calculation to get the talking time of the call!
2308: More info on Inbound calls lifecycle in the Webhook section.
2309: 2. Outbound calls
2310: Outbound calls are initiated by Agents from Aircall Workspace, calling an external person.
2311: If an Outbound call is not answered by the external person, the answered_at field will be null.
2312: The duration field is computed by the following: ended_at - started_at. As the ringing time is included in it, use the ended_at - answered_at calculation to get the talking time of the call. If an outbound call is answered by a voicemail, it will be considered as answered (Aircall does not support Answering Machine Detection yet).
2313: More info on Outbound calls lifecycle in the Webhook section.
2314: Starting an outbound call from Aircall Workspace is feasible
2315: with the Start Outbound Call endpoint, defined on the User object.
2316: 3. Internal calls
2317: Internal calls are initiated by an Agent, calling another Agent. Those calls are not rendered in the Public API.
2318: More info on how to use Intercall calls in our Knowledge Base.
2319: Call Comments (also called Notes)
2320: Calls can be commented by Agents or via the Public API endpoint [POST] /v1/calls/:id/comments.

2361: Fetch all Calls associated to a company and their information.
2362: By default, Calls are ordered by ascending IDs - consider using the order=desc query param if you want to get the last calls made by an account!
2363: Only six months of history is available. Please contact our Support team on support.aircall.io to get a one-time export of calls.

2370: String

2375: Default value is asc

2733: Search Calls
2734: Search for specific Calls depending on several Query Params like user_id, phone_number or tags. Given a call transferred between A and B phone numbers, the call will not appear when filtering by A but it will for B.
2735: Only six months of history is available. Please contact our Support team on support.aircall.io to get a one-time export of calls.
2736: By default contact details are not added in response payload. To add the contact details in response set fetch_contact to true in query parameters.

2891: Transfer a Call
2892: Calls can be transferred to another User, Team or phone number.
2893: Transfers initiated through the API are only supported for scenarios where a call is transferred directly to a specific agent.
2894: The transfer won’t reroute to other agents if the original transfer target is unavailable.
2895: For more complex scenarios -such as those requiring multiple sequential transfers or fallback routing— we
2896: recommend using the "Ring to via API" widget within Smartflows.
2897: This widget allows for advanced routing logic and provides greater flexibility in managing call flows.
2898: Only cold transfers are available via the Public API. Calls can be transferred to a single User, a single Team or a single external phone number:
2899: To transfer a Call to another User, provide a user ID in the request's body. A call.transferred Webhook event will be sent.
2900: If the agent to whom the call was transferred to is not available, call will be directed to the No one answers strategy: the Unanswered call message will be played.
2901: To transfer a Call to a Team, provide a team ID in the request's body. A call.transferred Webhook event will be sent.
2902: When transferring a call to a team, a dispatching strategy can be specified with parameter: dispatching_strategy:
2903: The "simultaneous" strategy (default one if argument is not specified) will ring each available member simultaneously.
2904: The "random" one will ring each available member one by one.
2905: The "longest_idle" one will ring each available member one by one starting with the agent having the longest idle time.
2906: To transfer an Incoming Call to an external phone number, provide a phone number in the request body. When transfer is initiated, a message will be played to the caller informing them that their call is being transferred. A call.transferred Webhook event will be sent without the transferred_to field in the payload.
2907: Transfers to external phone numbers will only work for inbound calls that have not yet been answered.
2908: If the transfer is not successful, a call.unsuccessful_transfer Webhook event will be sent.
2909: Path params
2910: id
2911: Integer
2912: Unique identifier for the Call.
2913: Body params
2914: user_id
2915: String
2916: Unique identifier of the User the Call will be transferred to.
2917: team_id
2918: String
2919: Unique identifier of the Team the Call will be transferred to.
2920: number
2921: String
2922: External phone number the Call will be transferred to.
2923: Format must be e164. More information in the dedicated phone numbers format section.
2924: dispatching_strategy
2925: String
2926: Specify dispatching strategy on team transfer, only values 'random', 'simultaneous' and 'longest_idle' are accepted. This parameter is optional if not specified 'simultaneous' strategy is implicitly used.
2927: Only one of user_id, team_id or number parameters are allowed for each request.
2928: code
2929: description
2930: 204
2931: Success.
2932: 400
2933: Call already ended.
2934: 400
2935: Invalid usage of dispatching strategy with user or external phone number.
2936: 400
2937: Multiple transfer destinies set on request.
2938: 404
2939: User or Call not found.
2940: Request
2941: POST /v1/calls/:id/transfers
2942: {
2943: "user_id": 456
2944: }

The concept of archiving a call is deprecated for Aircall Workspace users.
2999: Moving to Aircall Workspace? Workspace groups the calls and messages exchanged with the same contact on a Number into a Conversation, and agents close the Conversation when the work is done. Use Close a Conversation where you used to archive a Call. To find the Conversation of a Call, use List all Conversations with the call_id query param. To react when the work is done, as you did with call.archived, listen to the conversation.closed Webhook event.

3292: Conversation overview
3293: Limited availability: The Conversations endpoints and events are being rolled out gradually and aren't available to all Aircall accounts yet. If your account doesn't have access, requests to these endpoints won't work and the related webhook events won't be sent. To ask for access, please contact the Aircall Support team. We'll make this feature available to all accounts soon.
3294: In Aircall Workspace, calls and messages are grouped into Conversations. A Conversation belongs to one Number and one external party, such as a phone number or a WhatsApp user. It is either opened or closed, and it can be assigned to a User.
3295: Use the Conversation endpoints to find Conversations, to read their history, to close or reopen them, and to assign them to a teammate. You can also receive Conversation events as Webhooks.
3296: Unlike the Call object, the dates of a Conversation are ISO 8601 strings in UTC, for example 2026-10-01T09:12:44.000Z.

3353: List all Conversations
3354: Fetch all Conversations of a company, with the most recent ones first.
3355: The list covers the whole company. An API token is a company credential, so there is no restriction per user. Use the query params to narrow the list down.
3356: There is no endpoint to find a Conversation from a call or from a phone number. Use this endpoint instead:
3357: From a call: pass only call_id. It is a standalone lookup that returns the Conversation of this Call, or an empty list. All the other query params are ignored.
3358: From a phone number: filter with external_number, and optionally number_id or phone_number.
3359: Then use the id of the Conversation to retrieve, close, reopen or assign it. See the Conversation examples.
3360: Query params
3361: call_id
3362: Integer
3363: Standalone lookup. Returns the Conversation linked to this Call, or an empty list.
3364: All the other query params are ignored, and meta.per_page is 1. An empty value, or a value with non-digit characters, is rejected with a 400 HTTP code.
3365: status
3366: String
3367: Filter by the current status of the Conversation.
3368: Can be opened or closed. Any other value is rejected with a 400 HTTP code.
3369: phone_number
3370: String
3371: Filter on the Conversations of the Number with this phone number.
3372: Can be combined with number_id. An invalid format is rejected with a 400 HTTP code.
3373: external_number
3374: String
3375: Filter on the Conversations with this external number, on the other side of the Conversation.
3376: The formatting is ignored: +1 (555) 123-4567 and 15551234567 return the same Conversations. Special numbers are anonymous, intercom, client:<id>, airway_<id> and team:<id>. Any other value with no digit is rejected with a 400 HTTP code.
3377: number_id
3378: Integer
3379: Filter on the Conversations of this Number.
3380: Same value as the id of the Number. Can be combined with phone_number. Must be a positive whole number.

3383: Filter on the Conversations currently assigned to this User.
3384: Must be a positive whole number.
3385: from
3386: Integer

3639: Close a Conversation
3640: Closes an opened Conversation. This is the same action as when an agent closes a Conversation in Aircall Workspace.
3641: The body is optional. Use closed_by to name the User who closes the Conversation. Without it, the Conversation is closed by the system. The User is never taken from the API credentials.
3642: This endpoint is idempotent: closing a Conversation that is already closed returns a 200 HTTP code with the current Conversation, and has no side effect.
3643: Closing a Conversation that is assigned to a User also unassigns it.
3644: A conversation.closed Webhook event is sent when a Conversation is closed. More info in the Webhooks section.
3645: Looking for the replacement of Archive a Call? Closing a Conversation is how work is marked as done in Aircall Workspace. To find the Conversation of a Call, use List all Conversations with the call_id query param.
3646: See the Conversation examples to react to a closed Conversation in your own system.

3656: Optional. Must be a positive whole number and a User of your Company. Without it, the system closes the Conversation.

3752: Assign a Conversation
3753: Assigns a Conversation to a User, or reassigns it to another User.
3754: assigned_to is required. Use the optional assigned_by to name the User who makes the assignment. Without it, the assignment is made by the system. The User is never taken from the API credentials.
3755: This endpoint is idempotent: assigning a Conversation to its current assignee returns a 200 HTTP code with the current Conversation, and has no side effect.
3756: A closed Conversation cannot be assigned. Reopen it first, otherwise the request fails with a 422 HTTP code.
3757: A conversation.assigned Webhook event is sent when a Conversation is assigned. More info in the Webhooks section.

3819: Conversation examples
3820: A Conversation looks like the object on the right. The examples below show how to combine the Conversation endpoints and events.
3821: Example: close the Conversation of a Call
3822: Find the Conversation of the Call: GET /v1/conversations?call_id=812.
3823: Read the id of the Conversation in the response, for example 4321. An empty conversations list means the Call has no Conversation.
3824: Close the Conversation with this id: POST /v1/conversations/4321/close.
3825: Example: assign the Conversation with a phone number on one of your Numbers
3826: Find the opened Conversation with this external number on your Number: GET /v1/conversations?number_id=1234&external_number=%2B33612345678&status=opened.
3827: Read the id of the Conversation in the response, for example 4321.
3828: Assign the Conversation with this id: POST /v1/conversations/4321/assign with the body {"assigned_to": 456}.
3829: Example: list the opened Conversations assigned to a User
3830: GET /v1/conversations?status=opened&assigned_to=456
3831: Example: read the calls and messages of a Conversation
3832: List the Engagements of the Conversation, oldest first: GET /v1/conversations/4321/engagements?order=asc&per_page=50.
3833: For each Engagement, read its type. A call has a call_id, a message or whatsapp has a message_id. The other types record assignments, closes and reopens.
3834: While meta.next_page_link is not null, call it to get the next page.
3835: Example: create a helpdesk ticket when a Conversation is closed
3836: Close a Conversation and react to the event in your own system:
3837: A Conversation is closed: an agent closes it in Aircall Workspace, or your system calls Close a Conversation.
3838: Aircall sends a conversation.closed Webhook event to your server.
3839: Your server reads data.id and data.closed_at from the event, and creates a ticket in your helpdesk.
3840: If you need more details, call Retrieve a Conversation with data.id.
3841: Webhook events are delivered at least once. Make your server idempotent, as explained in Conversation events.

4027: Outbound Campaigns
4028: Overview
4029: Outbound Campaigns enables automated outbound dialing from a centrally managed contact list. A Campaign defines the list, dialing strategy and outcome labels. Multiple human agents or an AI Voice Agent are assigned to it, and the system handles call distribution automatically. Every attempt and outcome is tracked per contact.
4030: Outbound Campaigns is a distinct resource from Dialer Campaign, which covers the Power Dialer feature. A Dialer Campaign is agent-owned and manages a personal list of numbers dialled one at a time. A Campaign is admin-owned, supports multiple agents or an AI Voice Agent, and follows its own lifecycle (draft, in_progress, paused, completed, archived). The two resources are independent and do not share data.
4031: API tokens have company-wide access to Campaigns. Since tokens are admin-scoped by nature — and admins already have full visibility in the Dashboard — all campaigns are returned with no per-agent filtering applied.
4032: A Campaign has no overall contact limit. The synchronous Add Campaign contacts endpoint accepts up to 100 contacts per request. A contact import parses at most 10,000 data rows; a file with more rows fails outright, so split it across multiple imports.
4033: Error responses
4034: This section explains the error response shape and how clients should handle its fields; it is not an exhaustive catalogue of every error an endpoint can return. Errors from Outbound Campaigns requests follow a standard envelope format. Requests rejected upstream by the API gateway may return a shorter error response:
4035: {
4036: "error": "Unprocessable Entity",
4037: "message": "INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION",
4038: "errors": [
4039: {
4040: "status": 422,
4041: "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
4042: "detail": "UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY"
4043: }
4044: ],
4045: "troubleshoot": "Cannot transition campaign from \"completed\" to \"in_progress\"",
4046: "success": false
4047: }
4048: Use message to get the specific reason. Outbound Campaigns exposes stable semantic codes you can handle in your integration: INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION, CAMPAIGN_NOT_READY, CAMPAIGN_LAUNCH_REQUIRES_CALLER_ID_NUMBERS, CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION, OUTCOME_ALREADY_EXISTS, RESERVED_OUTCOME_NAME, OUTCOME_IN_USE, and BACKEND_API_UNREACHABLE.
4049: Use errors[].detail when you only need the HTTP category, such as BAD_REQUEST, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, or SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. Validation errors, opaque 404 responses, and errors without a recognised domain code also use this status-level constant in message. Internal library codes are never exposed, including numeric codes.
4050: AIVA campaigns
4051: Human and AI Voice Agent (AIVA) Campaigns follow the same lifecycle; all sections below apply to both unless noted. Choose the type at creation. agent_type cannot be changed later. AIVA Campaigns have specific rules for creation and contact payloads, described below.
4052: Create an AIVA campaign
4053: Set agent_type to aiva in Create a Campaign. Any field violation returns 400 with the field name:
4054: aiva_agent_id is required. The field is rejected when agent_type is not aiva.
4055: caller_id_strategy must be specific_number_pool, and caller_id_numbers must contain at least one number_id from List Campaign eligible numbers.
4056: calling_hours is required and is only valid for an AIVA Campaign. It contains an IANA timezone and between 1 and 10 slots. Each slot defines from_time, to_time (24-hour HH:MM), and days (MON–SUN). from_time must be earlier than to_time.
4057: agent_type is fixed at creation. Update a Campaign rejects that field; there is no endpoint for converting a human Campaign to AIVA or an AIVA Campaign to human.
4058: Human and AIVA Campaigns have separate company entitlements. A structurally valid create request can still return 422 when AIVA Campaigns are not enabled for the company.
4059: Add contacts to an AIVA campaign
4060: AIVA Campaign contacts only accept aiva_variables. Standard fields (first_name, last_name, email, company_name, note) are rejected — sending any returns 422 for the whole batch. Conversely, sending aiva_variables to a human Campaign also fails the whole batch with 422.
4061: On Add Campaign contacts, aiva_variables is a flat string-to-string map and its keys cannot be empty.
4062: Every context variable declared as required by the selected agent must be present and non-blank on every contact. A missing variable rejects that contact with reason: "variable_missing" — the rest of the batch is still queued. The response does not identify which variable is missing.
4063: Retrieve a Campaign returns the agent's context-variable contract, so you can discover it before building contact payloads. aiva_variable_keys lists the context variables the agent requires — the set an import's field_mapping.variables must cover — and aiva_optional_variable_keys lists the variables the agent accepts but never requires, any of which you may map. Both are null on a human Campaign and on an AIVA Campaign created before these fields existed; null means the contract is not recorded, never that the agent declares nothing.
4064: Bulk import AIVA contacts
4065: Use Add Campaign contacts for batches of up to 100 contacts. For larger batches, use the Campaign contact import CSV workflow.
4066: For an AIVA Campaign, field_mapping.variables is required when you create the import. It is an ordered array of { context_key, source_key } pairs and must cover every context variable the selected agent declares as required. If any required mapping is absent, the API returns 422 before creating the import and names the missing context_key values.
4067: The same agent-type separation as the inline endpoint applies to CSV mappings. An AIVA import must not map field_mapping.first_name, field_mapping.last_name, field_mapping.email, field_mapping.company_name or field_mapping.note; a 422 names the offending fields. Conversely, a human Campaign import must not carry field_mapping.variables; that is also a 422. field_mapping.phone_number remains required for both Campaign types because it identifies the number to dial.
4068: The variable mapping follows these rules:
4069: context_key: "phone_number" is reserved and silently dropped. Map the dialled number with the required field_mapping.phone_number field instead.
4070: Every context_key must be unique.
4071: Every source_key must be unique and must not reuse the column named by field_mapping.phone_number. csv_column is a deprecated alias for source_key: exactly one of the two is set per entry, and existing integrations sending csv_column keep working.
4072: Array order is preserved and sets the variable-column order of a later export.
4073: If the agent's configuration cannot be read, the import is refused rather than created.
4074: Worked example. This CSV maps a phone column and three required agent context variables:
4075: Phone,Customer ID,Plan,Renewal date
4076: +33612345678,cus_1042,Pro,2026-10-01
4077: +33698765432,cus_2084,Starter,2026-11-15
4078: Create the import with matching column names and the variables in the order you want a later export to use:
4079: Upload the CSV to the presigned upload.url from the response, following the form-field rules on Create a Campaign contact import. The valid rows then become contacts on the Campaign as the file is read; there is no review step and no second call. Poll the import to follow the run until it reports imported:
4080: Request
4081: GET /v1/campaigns/:id/contact_imports/:import_id
4082: Add "insertion_point": "start" to the create request instead if the imported contacts should go ahead of the contacts already waiting. See Retrieve a Campaign contact import for the status loop and for the counts of rows an AIVA import discarded.
4083: After contacts are queued, Launch the Campaign. The launch request requires the same compliance acknowledgment as a human Campaign.
4084: Request
4085: POST /v1/campaigns/:id/contact_imports
4086: {
4087: "file_name": "aiva-renewals.csv",
4088: "country_code": "FR",
4089: "field_mapping": {
4090: "phone_number": "Phone",
4091: "variables": [
4092: { "context_key": "customer_id", "source_key": "Customer ID" },
4093: { "context_key": "plan", "source_key": "Plan" },
4094: { "context_key": "renewal_date", "source_key": "Renewal date" }
4095: ]
4096: }
4097: }

4230: Set up a campaign
4231: Create a Campaign, then retrieve, list, update or delete it while it is still a draft. You can also duplicate an existing Campaign to start from its settings without copying its contacts.
4232: When setting up caller ID, List Campaign eligible numbers shows the numbers the company may use, while List Campaign lines reads the pool configured on a Campaign.
4233: Create a Campaign
4234: Create a Campaign in draft status.
4235: A draft Campaign is not live and has no dialling side effect: nothing is charged and no calls are placed until Launch a Campaign is called, which is what builds the call queue.
4236: Both kinds of Campaign can be created here: human agent (the default) and AI Voice Agent. Each is a separate per-company entitlement, so a body this endpoint accepts can still be refused with a 422 naming the one you are missing.
4237: A Campaign using caller_id_strategy: "specific_number_pool" must bring at least one entry in caller_id_numbers, or the request is a 400. Without numbers the Campaign could be created but never launched, so it is refused here rather than at launch. Pass the number_id values from List Campaign eligible numbers. Only ids: Aircall resolves the number itself, so an id your company cannot use for campaigns is rejected with a 400 naming it.
4238: This endpoint does not assign Users or Teams - those are separate write operations, each documented on its own page. An AI Voice Agent Campaign needs neither: it is refused if it has any.
4239: An AI Voice Agent Campaign, which must name its agent, dial from a specific number pool, and declare the hours it may call in:
4240: Request
4241: POST /v1/campaigns
4242: {
4243: "name": "Q3 outreach (AI Voice Agent)",
4244: "agent_type": "aiva",
4245: "aiva_agent_id": "8f1c2c9c-9b6b-4a11-9d9f-3ab01e2e4f1a",
4246: "caller_id_strategy": "specific_number_pool",
4247: "caller_id_numbers": [12345],
4248: "calling_hours": {
4249: "timezone": "America/New_York",
4250: "slots": [
4251: { "from_time": "09:00", "to_time": "18:00", "days": ["MON", "TUE", "WED", "THU", "FRI"] }
4252: ]
4253: }
4254: }

4315: 400

4318: One or more outcome_ids do not belong to your company's outcome catalogue.
4319: 422
4320: The agent_type you asked for is not enabled for your company. Human agent and AI Voice Agent Campaigns are separate per-company entitlements, so having one does not imply the other.

4483: Update a Campaign
4484: Update a Campaign's editable configuration.
4485: This is a partial update, despite the PUT verb. An omitted field is left untouched - it is not cleared or reset to a default. This API has no PATCH method, so PUT is reused for partial semantics rather than true replacement, which is not possible here anyway: status and end_date cannot be written by this or any endpoint.
4486: status is not editable here. Lifecycle changes go through the dedicated actions - Launch a Campaign, Pause a Campaign, Resume a Campaign, Archive a Campaign - each with its own preconditions and side effects.

4501: String

4503: Optional. One of agent_number_pool, specific_number_pool.

4505: Boolean

4507: Optional.

4511: Optional. Must be between 1 and 5.

4513: Integer

4515: Optional. Same floor and 259200s ceiling as on Create a Campaign.

4517: Integer
4518: How long, in seconds, a call rings before being considered unanswered.
4519: Optional. Must be between 1 and 3600.

4521: Integer
4522: How long, in seconds, an agent has to record a call outcome after a call ends.
4523: Optional. Must be between 1 and 3600.

4525: Array
4526: Which outcome tags (from List all Campaign Outcomes) agents can pick from when wrapping up a call on this Campaign.
4527: Optional. Each id must belong to your company's outcome catalogue, or the whole request is rejected with a 404. Unlike every other field here, [] and omitting the field mean different things: omitting it leaves the Campaign's outcomes untouched, [] removes every outcome from it.
4528: caller_id_numbers
4529: Array
4530: The Aircall numbers this Campaign may dial out from, as number_id values from List Campaign eligible numbers.
4531: Optional, and replaces the whole pool rather than adding to it: omit the field to leave the pool alone. Ids only - the number itself is resolved from your company's campaign-eligible set, so an ineligible id is a 400. caller_id_strategy is required whenever this field is sent - see the notice below.
4532: calling_hours
4533: Object
4534: The weekly window this Campaign may dial in - see Calling hours on the Campaign object for the full shape.
4535: Optional, and only on an AI Voice Agent Campaign that is still in draft. Send null to clear it. Attempting it on a human agent Campaign, or after the Campaign has left draft, is a 422.
4536: caller_id_numbers replaces the Campaign's pool: every number currently on it is removed and the ones you send are put in their place. To leave the pool untouched, omit the field.
4537: The two fields travel together in both directions. Sending caller_id_numbers requires caller_id_strategy, so it is always clear which strategy the pool is for - otherwise numbers sent to a Campaign currently on agent_number_pool would store a pool that does nothing until someone later switched the strategy and silently activated it. Setting caller_id_strategy to specific_number_pool does not require you to re-send the pool if the Campaign already has one - but it is refused with a 422 if the result would be a live Campaign on that strategy with no numbers, because it would have nothing to dial from. This applies to a draft too, not only a live Campaign: Create a Campaign refuses specific_number_pool without numbers, so the API would otherwise contradict itself and you would only discover the problem at launch. With agent_number_pool the array must be empty or absent. To change neither, omit both.
4538: On an AI Voice Agent Campaign, sending caller_id_numbers also triggers a fresh dialling pass over the new pool. That happens whenever the field is present, even if the numbers are identical to the ones already there, so avoid re-sending it from a periodic sync that has nothing to change.

4540: description
4541: 400
4542: A body field is out of range, carries an unknown key, caller_id_numbers was sent without caller_id_strategy, the two disagree (an empty array with specific_number_pool, or a non-empty one with agent_number_pool), or an id is not campaign-eligible for your company. agent_type, aiva_agent_id and run_mode are unknown keys here: each is fixed at creation, so they are rejected rather than silently ignored.

4544: No Campaign with this id in your company, or one or more outcome_ids do not belong to your company's outcome catalogue.
4545: 409
4546: The Campaign was modified concurrently by another request. Re-read the Campaign and retry. message is CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION.
4547: 422
4548: The Campaign's status does not allow editing. Only draft, in_progress and paused are editable; a completed or archived Campaign is refused. Also returned when calling_hours is sent to a human agent Campaign or to an AI Voice Agent Campaign that has already left draft, and when the change would leave the Campaign on specific_number_pool with no caller ID numbers, in any status.

4728: Add Campaign contacts
4729: Add up to 100 contacts to a Campaign and queue them for dialling in one request. A Campaign has no overall contact limit.
4730: This is the synchronous path, for feeding contacts in as they arrive. For larger volumes use the Campaign contact import flow instead, which uploads a CSV and processes it in the background.
4731: The contacts array in the response is positionally aligned to the one you sent: the first result describes your first contact, and so on. There is no index field. Read each result's status and, for a rejected contact, its reason at the same array position as the submitted contact.
4732: A successful response has no success key. HTTP 201 means at least one contact was queued. HTTP 200 can mean that every contact was rejected, so check queued_count, rejected_count and each positional result instead of treating every 2xx as a queued batch.
4733: Safe to retry. A replayed request queues nothing twice and changes nothing: within a Campaign a phone number identifies at most one contact, so every contact in the replay comes back as already_in_campaign. No idempotency key is needed.

4736: String

4740: String
4741: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region used to read numbers written in national format, e.g. FR turns 06 12 34 56 78 into 33612345678.
4742: Required, with no default. A wrong region does not fail loudly - it produces valid-looking numbers for another country, and the first sign of trouble is calls placed to strangers. Numbers already in full international form are unaffected. A well-formed but non-existent region such as ZZ is rejected with 400.
4743: position
4744: String
4745: Where the contacts land in the existing queue: top or bottom.
4746: Optional, defaults to bottom. top puts them ahead of everyone already waiting. Note this differs from Create a Campaign contact import, which spells the same idea insertion_point with start/end.
4747: contacts
4748: Array
4749: The contacts to add. Between 1 and 100 elements.
4750: Required. More than 100 is rejected with 400; use the Campaign contact import flow for larger lists.

4752: String
4753: The number to dial. National or international format; read against country_code.
4754: Required.
4755: contacts[].first_name
4756: String
4757: The contact's first name.
4758: Optional. Human agent Campaigns only.
4759: contacts[].last_name
4760: String

4762: Optional. Human agent Campaigns only.
4763: contacts[].email
4764: String
4765: The contact's email address.
4766: Optional. Human agent Campaigns only.
4767: contacts[].company_name
4768: String
4769: The contact's company name.
4770: Optional. Human agent Campaigns only.
4771: contacts[].note
4772: String
4773: Free-text note to store with the contact.
4774: Optional. Human agent Campaigns only.
4775: contacts[].aiva_variables
4776: Object
4777: Context passed to the AI Voice Agent for this contact, as string keys to string values, e.g. {"plan": "Pro"}.
4778: AIVA Campaigns only. Every context variable the agent declares as required must be present with a non-blank value. The agent's optional context-variable declarations are not required and are ignored when the Campaign validates a contact. Extra keys are accepted and passed through. Keys must be non-empty.
4779: The accepted fields depend on the Campaign's agent type, and mixing them fails the whole request with 422. An AIVA Campaign accepts aiva_variables only; a human agent Campaign accepts the five descriptive fields only. Both accept phone_number.
4780: On an AIVA Campaign, a contact must carry every context variable the agent declares as required, each with a non-blank value. A contact missing one is reported individually as variable_missing rather than failing the request, so the rest of the batch can still be queued. The agent's optional context variables are not required and are ignored by Campaign validation. Extra keys are accepted and passed through to the agent.

4886: Remove a Campaign contact
4887: Remove one contact from a Campaign's queue, so it will not be dialled. This is the undo of Add Campaign contacts.
4888: The contact is addressed by its phone number, which is its identity within a Campaign - a contact has no id of its own. Feed back a phone_number exactly as List Campaign contacts returns it and it matches by construction.
4889: Removing a contact also removes its queue item. The two are one thing from the outside: a contact is only in a Campaign because something is queued to dial it.
4890: Removal has one of two effects.
4891: Delete. A contact with no recorded attempts is deleted with no call history.
4892: Cancel next attempts. If the contact has at least one recorded attempt, any remaining retries are cancelled and the contact leaves the queue. The latest known outcome, when one exists, is kept and made final so it remains available in the Campaign's outcomes. The API does not create a cancellation outcome.

4894: id
4895: String
4896: Unique identifier for the Campaign (UUID).
4897: phone_number
4898: String
4899: The contact's phone number, as returned by List Campaign contacts. Lenient about formatting: 33612345678, +33612345678 and +33 6 12 34 56 78 all address the same contact. Percent-encode the + as %2B in the path. A national number such as 0612345678 cannot be used - it is only resolvable against a country, and an API token is company-wide with no country attached.

4906: 404
4907: No Campaign with this id in your company, or no contact with this phone number in it. Deliberately not an idempotent 204: a mistyped number stays distinguishable from a real removal.

4912: Campaign queue items
4913: A Campaign's dial queue, in dial order: list it to see who's next and how the last attempt on each went, reorder an item to change its position, or reschedule one to change when it's next attempted. List Campaign contacts answers who is in the queue; this answers what order and when.
4914: List Campaign queue items
4915: Fetch a Campaign's dial queue, in dial order. List Campaign contacts answers who is in the Campaign and Retrieve Campaign statistics answers the aggregate; this answers what order they will be called in and how the last attempt on each went.
4916: Deliberately narrow. Scheduler internals - retry counters, the next intended attempt time, and the derived live-queue display state - are not published here, to avoid freezing today's retry model into the contract.
4917: Paged by cursor like every other collection on this API, but the cursor encodes queue position rather than creation time, because the queue is ordered by position. This is invisible to a client - the cursor is opaque either way - but a cursor from this endpoint is not interchangeable with one from another.

5079: Campaign contact import
5080: The CSV workflow for loading contacts into a Campaign's dial queue, in two steps: create an import and get a presigned upload target, then retrieve it to follow the file as its valid rows are added to the Campaign. There is no separate call to queue the contacts, and nothing else to read: the import itself carries the whole summary.
5081: For an AIVA Campaign, the create step must map CSV columns to every required agent context variable. See the end-to-end AIVA Campaign bulk-import example.
5082: There is no review step. An uploaded file is imported directly: the valid rows become Campaign contacts and join the dial queue as they are parsed, so a wrong file queues real calls to real people. There is no undo once dialling starts - inspect the file before uploading it.
5083: Contact import status lifecycle
5084: Every import starts at pending and moves through the states below. imported, failed and stopped are terminal.
5085: status
5086: meaning
5087: pending
5088: The import exists and the upload target has been issued, but the CSV has not reached it. Nothing is queued yet. A file that never arrives, or arrives after upload.expires_at, moves the import to failed.
5089: processing
5090: The file arrived and is being read. Each batch of valid rows is added to the Campaign as it is parsed, so the contacts of a processing import are already in the dial queue.
5091: imported
5092: Every row has been read. All valid rows are Campaign contacts; invalid and duplicate rows were discarded.
5093: failed
5094: The import stopped on an error - an upload that never arrived, an unreadable file, or a run that lost its worker. Any contacts added before the failure stay in the queue. The response does not say which error it was.
5095: stopped
5096: The import was stopped from the Aircall dashboard before it finished reading the file. Contacts added before the stop stay in the queue.
5097: A failed or stopped import is a partial import, not an undone one. The import's own counts say how far it got - valid_count rows are Campaign contacts, invalid_count and duplicate_count were discarded - so import only the rest.
5098: ready, promoting and promoted are not part of this lifecycle. An import created before CSV imports became direct still reports them rather than an invented state; nothing new is created that way.
5099: Create a Campaign contact import
5100: The way to load a CSV file of contacts into a Campaign: create the import and get somewhere to upload the file. Once the file is uploaded and read, its valid rows become contacts on the Campaign and join its dial queue - there is no review step and no second call to queue them. Retrieve a Campaign contact import reports the progress. A Campaign has no overall contact limit. One import parses at most 10,000 data rows; a file with more rows fails outright, so split it across multiple imports.
5101: The file does not go through this endpoint or through api.aircall.io at all. The response carries a presigned upload target; your integration uploads the CSV directly there as multipart/form-data, with fields sent exactly as returned, in order, and the file part last.
5102: The uploaded file is imported directly. There is no review step between parsing and dialling: as each batch of rows is read, the valid ones are added to the Campaign and queued, so a wrong file puts real calls in front of real people. Check the file before uploading, not after.
5103: One import in flight per Campaign. Creating a second one while an earlier import is still pending or processing fails with 422 - imports cannot be pipelined.
5104: Add a separate form field literally named Content-Type, with the value from upload.content_type (currently always text/csv), before the file part. S3's upload policy checks this field, not the MIME Content-Type: header on the file part itself - omitting it fails the upload with a 403 AccessDenied ("Policy Condition failed") even though the file part's own header is correct.
5105: An AIVA Campaign requires field_mapping.variables to map CSV columns to every context variable its agent declares as required. A missing required mapping returns 422, names the missing context_key values, and creates no import. See the complete AIVA bulk-import example.
5106: The mapping fields must match the Campaign's agent type. An AIVA import rejects field_mapping.first_name, field_mapping.last_name, field_mapping.email, field_mapping.company_name and field_mapping.note with 422 naming the offending fields. A human Campaign import rejects field_mapping.variables with 422. field_mapping.phone_number is required for both.

5251: Retrieve a Campaign contact import
5252: Poll this after uploading the CSV, while an import's status is pending or processing; stop at imported, failed or stopped. That loop is guaranteed to terminate - a stuck worker surfaces as failed rather than as processing forever.
5253: This reports an import, not a queue. The import adds each valid row to the Campaign as the file is read, so a processing import has already queued contacts: failed and stopped do not undo them.
5254: The full import summary is here: status, the four counts and the timestamps. There are no per-row results to fetch alongside it - an import is read and applied batch by batch and keeps only the counts.

5769: Run the campaign
5770: Launch a Campaign to start dialling, then pause and resume it while it runs. Retrieve Campaign statistics reports its progress.
5771: A Campaign with run_mode: "one_time" (the default) reaches completed automatically after its contacts are resolved. A run_mode: "continuous" Campaign never auto-completes: when its queue drains it stays in_progress and dials whatever contacts are added later, until you pause it, or pause and then archive it. It cannot return from completed to an active or editable state; the only available transition is to archived. Archive is irreversible.
5772: Launch a Campaign
5773: Take a draft Campaign live. This builds the call queue from the Campaign's contacts and moves its status to in_progress - the only action that does either, which is why it is a separate endpoint from Pause, Resume and Archive.
5774: A run_mode: "one_time" Campaign needs at least one contact to launch. A run_mode: "continuous" Campaign can be launched with an empty queue - it stays live and dials contacts as they are added.
5775: Every launch requires compliance_acknowledged: true, for both human and AI Voice Agent Campaigns. By setting it, you attest that your company has the right to dial every contact in the Campaign and accepts responsibility for consent, do-not-call rules and calling hours. Omitting the field is a 400; sending false is a 422 and does not launch the Campaign.

5909: Archive a Campaign
5910: Move a Campaign to archived. Unlike Delete a Campaign, an archived Campaign stays visible and reportable - archiving is a lifecycle state, not a removal.
5911: Archiving is irreversible. An archived Campaign has no outgoing transition and can never be deleted, resumed, relaunched or returned to another state. Delete a draft before archiving it if you need to remove it. Use Pause instead if the Campaign may run again.
5912: Only a Campaign in draft, paused or completed status can be archived. An in_progress Campaign must be paused first. A completed Campaign cannot return to an active or editable state; archiving is its only outgoing transition.
5913: Unlike Pause, Archive does not end agent sessions. It refuses while any session is still active or paused, so a session cannot be stranded on an archived Campaign.

6004: Record the result
6005: Manage the company-wide Campaign Outcome catalogue of custom disposition labels. Outcomes are either applied automatically by the system or logged manually by an agent during wrap-up. For calls placed on a specific Campaign, list its call outcomes to retrieve all recorded outcomes, including both system-applied and agent-provided results. An external system can also record an outcome through the API.
6006: A Campaign Outcome is a reusable catalogue entry. A Campaign call outcome is the disposition recorded against one call attempt. The similar names describe different resources.
6007: The Campaign Outcome object
6008: A Campaign Outcome is a company-defined call disposition - a custom label an agent (or an external system, through the API) can attach to a Campaign call attempt to record how it went, alongside Aircall's own built-in outcomes like voicemail or unanswered.
6009: Outcomes are defined once per company and reused across every Campaign - this is why the resource is company-scoped at /v1/campaign_outcomes rather than nested under a single Campaign.
6010: This resource exists to complete a reference that already shipped: List Campaign call outcomes can return outcome: { "type": "custom", "id": "...", "name": "...", "color": "..." } for an attempt disposed with a custom outcome. This is that outcome's own catalogue entry, addressable by the same id.
6011: An API token has company-wide access to Campaign Outcomes, the same as every other resource on this surface - a token can see, create, update and delete every outcome in the company.

6020: String

6022: Can be null when unset.

6124: Delete a Campaign Outcome
6125: Soft-delete a Campaign Outcome. The row is marked deleted and disappears from every read path - the same effect as deleting from the dashboard. Its name becomes reusable by a new outcome immediately afterwards.
6126: An outcome cannot be deleted while it is still linked to a non-deleted Campaign, or while at least one call attempt has already recorded it - even one on a Campaign this outcome is no longer linked to. There is no way to force it: unlink the Campaign(s) first, but a recorded attempt is permanent, so an outcome that has ever been used on a real call can never be deleted afterwards.

6359: Record a Campaign call outcome
6360: Record the disposition of a call attempt that has already ended - what an agent would pick in the wrap-up UI, set by an external system instead.
6361: This can only touch a call that has already ended. An attempt that is still in progress is refused with a 422.
6362: Recording an outcome replaces any outcome already on the attempt - last write wins, with no check for whether one is already present. This lets a caller correct a previous mis-recording, but it also means a blind retry of a request that already succeeded can overwrite whatever was set in between (see the 409 below).
6363: The call attempt must belong to the Campaign named by id. A wrong or nonexistent Campaign id returns the same 404 as a missing or cross-company attempt, and no outcome is recorded.
6364: The response reuses the same call outcome shape returned by GET /v1/campaigns/{id}/call_outcomes.
6365: Path params
6366: id
6367: String
6368: Unique identifier for the Campaign (UUID).
6369: Body params
6370: call_id
6371: Integer
6372: The Aircall Call id, as returned by GET /v1/calls.
6373: Mandatory field.
6374: outcome_id
6375: String
6376: A company-defined outcome id, from List all Campaign Outcomes.
6377: Provide exactly one of outcome_id or predefined_outcome.
6378: predefined_outcome
6379: String
6380: A built-in outcome code.
6381: One of do_not_call, wrong_number. These are the only predefined codes settable this way - the rest (unanswered, voicemail, etc.) are set by the dialler from what happened on the line, not chosen by whoever records a disposition.
6382: is_final
6383: Boolean
6384: Whether this outcome ends the contact's retry sequence.
6385: Optional. Ignored for a predefined_outcome - do_not_call and wrong_number are always final. Defaults to true for a custom outcome.
6386: code
6387: description
6388: 400
6389: A malformed body: unknown key, missing call_id, neither or both of outcome_id and predefined_outcome provided, or a predefined_outcome that is not one of the settable codes.
6390: 404
6391: No attempt with that call_id under this Campaign in your company, or an outcome_id that does not exist in your company. A wrong or nonexistent Campaign id produces the same response.
6392: 409
6393: The attempt changed concurrently, for example because an agent recorded an outcome at the same moment. Re-read List Campaign call outcomes before retrying; a blind retry would overwrite what they set. message is CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION.
6394: 422
6395: The attempt exists but has not ended yet, so there is nothing to record against.
6396: 503
6397: The retry could not be scheduled. The outcome is already committed when this happens - re-read before deciding whether to retry.

6400: {

6403: }

7637: Trackers
7638: Conversation Trackers let you monitor calls matching keyword-based criteria you define — for example, calls containing specific terms, in a given direction, on a specific line, or handled by specific agents.
7639: The Tracker object is not creatable, updatable, nor destroyable via Aircall Public API.
7640: The Tracker object and APIs can only be retrieved if a company has signed up for Aircall AI Package with AI Assist or AI Assist Pro.
7641: Attributes
7642: id
7643: Integer
7644: Unique identifier for the Tracker.
7645: title
7646: String
7647: Name of the Tracker.
7648: type
7649: String
7650: Type of the Tracker.
7651: Currently only keywords is supported.
7652: created_at
7653: String
7654: Timestamp when the Tracker was created, in UTC.
7655: created_by
7656: Integer
7657: Unique identifier of the User who created the Tracker.
7658: updated_at
7659: String
7660: Timestamp when the Tracker was last updated, in UTC.
7661: null if the Tracker has never been updated.
7662: updated_by
7663: Integer
7664: Unique identifier of the User who last updated the Tracker.
7665: null if the Tracker has never been updated.
7666: filters
7667: Object
7668: Matching criteria for the Tracker.
7669: See Filters section below for more details.
7670: Filters
7671: The filters object defines which calls match a Tracker.
7672: Attributes
7673: query_terms
7674: Array[String]
7675: Terms a call must match.
7676: null if not set.
7677: exclude_query_terms
7678: Array[String]
7679: Terms a call must not match.
7680: null if not set.
7681: call_direction
7682: String
7683: Direction a call must match.
7684: Can be inbound or outbound. null if not set.
7685: speaker_type
7686: String
7687: Who must have said the matched terms.
7688: Can be agent or external. null if not set.
7689: line_ids
7690: Array[Integer]
7691: Numbers a call must be on.
7692: null if not set.
7693: agent_ids
7694: Array[Integer]
7695: Users a call must involve.
7696: null if not set.

7736: Retrieve a Tracker
7737: Retrieve details of a specific Tracker, including the calls that currently match its filters.
7738: This endpoint requires the AI Assist Pro or AI Assist package to be enabled for your company.
7739: Path params
7740: tracker_id
7741: Integer
7742: Unique identifier for the Tracker.
7743: Each entry in the calls array represents a call matching the Tracker's filters.
7744: Attributes
7745: call_id
7746: Integer
7747: Unique identifier for the Call.
7748: start_time
7749: String
7750: Timestamp when the Call started, in UTC (ISO 8601).
7751: Not to be confused with the start_time query parameter below, which is a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
7752: duration_seconds
7753: Integer
7754: Duration of the Call, in seconds.
7755: direction
7756: String
7757: Direction of the Call.
7758: Can be inbound or outbound.
7759: The query parameters below filter the calls matched to the Tracker.
7760: Query params
7761: start_time
7762: Integer
7763: Set a minimal date for matched calls (Unix timestamp in milliseconds).
7764: Optional field. Defaults to 7 days before end_time. Must not be after end_time or in the future.
7765: end_time
7766: Integer
7767: Set a maximal date for matched calls (Unix timestamp in milliseconds).
7768: Optional field. Defaults to now. Must not be in the future.
7769: direction
7770: String
7771: Filter matched calls by direction.
7772: Optional field. Can be inbound or outbound.
7773: agent_ids
7774: String
7775: Filter matched calls by User id(s).
7776: Optional field. Comma-separated integers, e.g. 123,456.
7777: line_ids
7778: String
7779: Filter matched calls by Number id(s).
7780: Optional field. Comma-separated integers, e.g. 123,456.
7781: next_token
7782: String
7783: Pagination cursor for matched calls.
7784: Optional field. Pass the meta.next_token value from the previous response.
7785: limit
7786: Integer
7787: Number of matched calls to return per page.
7788: Optional field. Default value is 20. Maximum is 50.
7789: start_time and end_time are Unix timestamps in milliseconds, not seconds.

7837: Content are not updatable nor destroyable via Aircall Public API.
7838: Content information is only present in transcriptions, summaries, topics, action items and it can be accessed inside the conversation intelligence object

7884: Message
7885: Message overview
7886: Messages including SMS, MMS, and WhatsApp are an essential part of how Aircall users interact with the product. Our mission is to make the communication experience as delightful as possible!
7887: There are two types of messages:
7888: Inbound Messages: when a user receives a message from an external person.
7889: Outbound Messages: when a user sends a message to an external person.
7890: Message objects are neither updatable nor destroyable via Aircall Public API.
7891: The attributes specific for whatsapp won’t be present if this is an SMS or MMS.
7892: Usage limits
7893: Aircall enforces per-line volume limits on outbound SMS, in addition to the overall API rate limit. Limits depend on the number's country and type:
7894: number type
7895: hourly
7896: daily
7897: monthly
7898: US / CA long code & toll-free
7899: 5,000
7900: 10,000
7901: 100,000
7902: UK / AU / DE / ES, and FR platform
7903: 500
7904: 2,000
7905: 20,000
7906: FR mobile
7907: 100
7908: 1,000
7909: 10,000
7910: WhatsApp messaging limits are not fixed by Aircall. They are set by the messaging tier Meta assigns to each WhatsApp-capable number, and increase automatically as the number sends compliant, high-quality traffic. You can check a number's current tier with Get WhatsApp Line Status.

7986: Message Callbacks
7987: When a number is configured using the Create Number Configuration endpoint with a callbackUrl, Aircall will POST callback payloads to that URL for two events:
7988: message.received — an inbound message arrived on the number.
7989: message.updated — the delivery status of an outbound message changed.
7990: Callbacks are distinct from Aircall Webhooks. Callbacks are sent to the URL configured via the Create Number Configuration endpoint.
7991: Delivery semantics
7992: Aircall expects a 2xx HTTP response within 5 seconds. There is no automatic retry on failure. The token field in the payload can be used to verify the request comes from Aircall.

7994: attributes-field
7995: type
7996: description
7997: resource
7998: String
7999: Always "message".
8000: event_name
8001: String
8002: Either "message.received" or "message.updated".
8003: timestamp
8004: Integer
8005: Unix timestamp of the event in milliseconds.
8006: token
8007: String
8008: The token returned when the number configuration was created. Use it to authenticate incoming requests.
8009: data
8010: Object
8011: A Message object plus the additional fields below.
8012: Additional fields in data
8013: The data object contains the standard Message attributes plus the following callback-specific ones:

8016: String
8017: Error description when a message fails. Format: "Code <code> (<description>)".
8018: Only present on failed message.updated callbacks.

8021: WhatsApp-specific metadata. Only present for WhatsApp messages. See The whatsapp object below.
8022: Only present for WhatsApp messages.

8589: High Volume Messages
8590: High Volume Messages overview
8591: High Volume Messages endpoints are designed for automated, high-throughput, or non-conversational sending — such as notifications, alerts, and campaigns — where messages are sent directly to recipients without being stored in an agent's Aircall inbox.
8592: Before sending, a number must be registered using the Create Number Configuration endpoint. Messages sent through these endpoints do not appear in the agent workspace; for conversational, agent-visible messaging, use the endpoints under Message instead.
8593: Create Number Configuration
8594: Create or update the number configuration to allow a number to use the Send Message Skipping Aircall Inbox or Send WhatsApp Message Skipping Aircall Inbox endpoints.
8595: Use the type field to specify whether the number is being configured for SMS (sms the default) or WhatsApp (whatsapp).
8596: Once numbers are configured, they won't be able to send or receive messages via Aircall apps.
8597: Numbers meant to be used with Send message in agent conversation or Send WhatsApp Message in Agent Conversation do not require to be configured.
8598: For US long codes and US/CA toll free lines, numbers must be registered before SMS configuration. See here to check registration status.
8599: Set a callbackURL that will be used not only to retrieve the status of messages sent, but also to get the messages received. Webhooks to retrieve messages activity do not expose messages sent and received with numbers that are active using the configuration exposed in this section. See Message Callbacks for the full payload structure and examples.

8862: Send WhatsApp Message Skipping Aircall Inbox
8863: Send a WhatsApp message (text, media, or template) from a WhatsApp-capable number directly to a recipient, without storing the message in the Aircall agent inbox.
8864: This endpoint is designed for high-volume or non-conversational use cases, such as notifications or automated messages. For conversational use cases where agents need visibility, use Send WhatsApp Message in Agent Conversation.
8865: Licence requirement: The company must have an active whatsapp_messaging addon. If the addon is not active, the request will be rejected with a 403 error. Contact your Aircall account manager to enable this addon.
8866: You can send one of the following per request:
8867: - A text message (text)
8868: - A media message (mediaUrl)
8869: - A template message (templateParams)
8870: Providing both text/mediaUrl and templateParams in the same request is not allowed.
8871: Body params
8872: lineId
8873: Integer
8874: Unique identifier for the WhatsApp-capable Number.
8875: Mandatory field
8876: to
8877: String
8878: Recipient phone number in E.164 format.
8879: Mandatory field
8880: text
8881: String
8882: Text message body (max 4096 characters). Mutually exclusive with templateParams. Can only be sent within an open 24-hour conversation window. Outside the window, use templateParams to initiate contact. Sending text outside the window returns 200 but delivers error 63016 to your registered webhook.
8883: Optional field
8884: mediaUrl
8885: String (URI)
8886: Publicly accessible media URL to send. Mutually exclusive with templateParams.
8887: Optional field

8889: Object

8891: Optional field

8894: Unique identifier of the WhatsApp template to use. Retrieve available template IDs from the List WhatsApp Templates endpoint.
8895: Mandatory when templateParams is present

8897: Array<Object>
8898: Variable substitutions for the template body. Each item must have key (String) and value (String).
8899: Optional field
8900: templateParams.buttons
8901: Array<Object>
8902: Variable substitutions for template buttons. Each item must have key (String) and value (String).
8903: Optional field
8904: templateParams.header
8905: Object
8906: Variable substitution for the template header component (image, document, or video URL). Required only for templates that include a media header.
8907: Optional field

8974: Contact
8975: Contact overview
8976: Contacts are a core part of Aircall experience.
8977: Every time Agents are on a call, Aircall fetches their contact information from different sources.
8978: Please note that contacts created by third-party integrations will not be accessible from the public-api, but you will still be able to see them in Aircall Workspace
8979: To better understand how contacts sync from third-party integrations works, you can have a look at this article from our knowledge base.
8980: Contacts CSV files can be uploaded by Agents in Aircall Workspace.
8981: More info here.

9717: Webhook
9718: Webhook API overview
9719: This section describes only REST endpoints related to Webhooks.
9720: If you want to know more about Webhook events and how to use them, please refer to this section.
9721: Aircall Public API allows any developer to fetch, create, update and delete Webhooks for an Aircall account.
9722: With OAuth, only the webhook linked to the token is accessible.
9723: With Basic Auth, webhooks created through the Aircall's dashboard and Basic Auth API requests are accessible.
9724: Webhooks are mainly composed of a custom_name and a list of events (see full events list here).
9725: Use the token field to identify from which Aircall account a Webhook is sent from!

9902: If the events field is not specified, Webhook will be registered to all events by default. If you don't want the events array to be overridden by the default value then please specify query param events_action=add.

10336: Trigger an Outbound Call
10337: An Outbound Voice Agent places calls to contacts on behalf of your company. Instead of answering incoming calls, the agent proactively dials out — triggered by an external system like a CRM, scheduling tool, or automation platform via this endpoint.
10338: Common use cases include appointment reminders, billing follow-ups, post-service surveys, and lead qualification.
10339: Before using this endpoint, configure your Outbound Voice Agent in the Aircall Dashboard. The agent must have a connected phone number and a first message defined.
10340: Outbound calls are subject to the limits below. Requests are queued until a slot is available; if expiration_seconds elapses before a slot opens, the call is dropped and never placed.
10341: limit
10342: value
10343: notes
10344: API rate limit
10345: 120 requests / minute / company
10346: Standard Aircall API rate limit. Caps how fast requests can be submitted; accepted requests are queued and placed when concurrency allows.
10347: Per-company concurrency
10348: 5 concurrent calls
10349: Maximum outbound agent calls a single company can have in flight at any time.
10350: Per-number concurrency
10351: 1 concurrent call
10352: Each agent has a dedicated phone number (1:1); that number can only host one live call at a time.
10353: Path params
10354: agent_id
10355: String
10356: Unique identifier for the Outbound Voice Agent.
10357: Can be found in the Outbound Call Workflow tab of the agent's configuration page.
10358: Body params
10359: contact_phone
10360: String
10361: The phone number to call, with country code. Leading + is optional. Spaces, dashes, and parentheses are stripped automatically.
10362: Mandatory field. Examples: +15551234567, 15551234567, +1 (555) 123-4567.
10363: idempotency_key
10364: String
10365: A unique identifier for this call request. Sending the same key twice will not create a duplicate call.
10366: Mandatory field. Use something meaningful like campaign-{date}-{customer_id}. A key cannot be reused even if the original request failed — generate a new key for each retry.
10367: context
10368: Object
10369: Key-value pairs that fill in {{variable}} placeholders in the agent's first message, voicemail message, and conversation guidelines. See Template Variables for details.
10370: Every {{variable}} in the first message and voicemail message must have a corresponding key — otherwise the call is rejected. Variables in the conversation guidelines are optional.
10371: expiration_seconds
10372: Integer
10373: How long (in seconds) the system will keep trying to place the call if the concurrency limit is reached.
10374: Min: 60. Max: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 3600 (1 hour).
10375: code
10376: description
10377: 202
10378: Call request accepted and queued.
10379: 400
10380: Invalid request. Missing template variables, invalid phone number format, or other validation error. Check error_message in the response.
10381: 403
10382: Outbound calling is not enabled for this company.
10383: 404
10384: Agent not found. Verify the agent ID is correct.
10385: 409
10386: Duplicate idempotency key, or agent does not have a phone number assigned.
10387: 422
10388: Missing required field (contact_phone or idempotency_key).
10389: 500

10391: 503

10412: Template Variables
10413: The context object in the Trigger an Outbound Call request provides values for any {{variable}} placeholders used in the agent's first message, voicemail message, or conversation guidelines.
10414: location
10415: variable type
10416: if missing from context
10417: First message
10418: Required
10419: The call is rejected with 400.
10420: Voicemail message
10421: Required
10422: The call is rejected with 400.
10423: Conversation guidelines
10424: Optional
10425: The call is placed; the agent proceeds without that value.
10426: Required variables: Every {{variable}} in the first message and voicemail message must have a corresponding key in context. The value is substituted directly into the message before it is spoken.
10427: Optional variables: {{variable}} placeholders in the conversation guidelines are not substituted as literal text. Instead, every key in context is shared with the agent as information about the contact, and the agent uses those values wherever the guidelines reference them. Use optional variables for details that improve the conversation but are not needed to start it, such as an account tier or a recent order. If an optional variable may not always be provided, write the guidelines so they still make sense without it (for example, "If you know the customer's last order, mention it.").
10428: Keys in context that are not referenced by any template are still shared with the agent as information about the contact.
10429: Variable names can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores — no spaces (e.g. {{first_name}}, not {{first name}}).
10430: Values can be strings, numbers, or dates.
10431: Datetime handling: If a context value is a UTC datetime in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-20T14:30:00Z), the system automatically converts it to natural language. In this case, a timezone key is required in the context so the system knows what local time to use.
10432: If the datetime includes an offset (e.g., 2024-03-20T10:30:00-04:00), no timezone key is needed. You can also pass dates pre-formatted as plain strings.

10439: IANA timezone identifier for datetime conversion.
10440: Required when a context value is a UTC datetime (e.g., 2024-03-20T14:30:00Z). Not needed if datetime includes an offset or is pre-formatted. Example: America/New_York.

10456: Each outbound call request creates an event that progresses through these statuses:
10457: Attributes
10458: PENDING
10459: String
10460: The call request has been accepted and is queued.
10461: INITIATED
10462: String
10463: The call has been placed and the phone is ringing.
10464: IN_PROGRESS
10465: String
10466: Someone or something answered and the agent is actively on the call.
10467: COMPLETED
10468: String
10469: The call has finished.
10470: Call outcome (e.g., human answered, voicemail, no answer) is available in the notes section of the call in the Conversation Center.
10471: FAILED
10472: String
10473: The call could not be completed due to network issues, timeouts, or repeated failed attempts.
10474: On system failures, the call is automatically reattempted, provided the call did not fail mid-conversation.
10475: REJECTED

10481: Analytics
10482: Analytics overview
10483: The Analytics API exposes Aircall's analytics data through the public API as asynchronous exports. Generating a report is a two-step flow:
10484: Create an export job with Create an Analytics Report Export. The response returns an exportID and a status of PENDING.
10485: Poll Retrieve an Analytics Report Export until the status becomes COMPLETED (or FAILED). When complete, the response includes a presigned downloadUrl you can use to fetch the file.
10486: Twelve report types are supported, covering call history, user status history, and a range of user-activity breakdowns. The set of filters available is the same regardless of the report type; only the resulting file's columns differ. End-to-end completion typically takes seconds to a few minutes depending on the date range and report.
10487: Exports are always scoped to the authenticated company — you cannot retrieve data for other companies.
10488: The Analytics API requires the Analytics+ entitlement on the company. Requests from companies without this entitlement are rejected with a 403.
10489: The downloadUrl returned on a completed export is a presigned, time-limited URL. Once downloadUrlExpiresAt has passed, the link stops working — re-call the retrieve endpoint to obtain a fresh URL while the export remains available.

10567: Create an Analytics Report Export
10568: Submit a new asynchronous export job for one of the supported Analytics report types. The response returns an exportID you can use to poll the job with Retrieve an Analytics Report Export.
10569: The filter object is shared across all report types — only the resulting file's columns change with reportName. Provide exactly one of filter.dateFilter.relative or filter.dateFilter.absoluteRange to scope the date window. Exports are always scoped to the authenticated company; you cannot query data for other companies.
10570: This endpoint requires the Analytics+ entitlement. Requests from companies without this entitlement are rejected with 403.
10571: Instead of polling Retrieve an Analytics Report Export, you can subscribe to the analytics.report_created and analytics.report_failed webhook events to be notified when the job completes.
10572: Date ranges are silently clipped when they exceed retention boundaries — no error is returned. For CALLS_HISTORY, dates older than 6 months are clipped to the boundary; for USER_STATUS_HISTORY, dates older than 7 days are clipped. Always verify the date range covered by the output CSV before relying on the data.
